questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, during execution the PM directs and manages project work, develops the team, manages stakeholder engagement, conducts procurements, and manages communications. Most of the budget is spent during this phase.

questions.question: A project team member is underperforming. The PM should FIRST:
options: A. Immediately remove them from the project
B. Have a private conversation to understand the issue and offer support
C. Report them to HR for termination
D. Ignore the problem and hope it improves
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, effective team management starts with understanding the root cause of underperformance. The PM should have a private, constructive conversation, identify barriers, provide support or training, and set clear expectations.

questions.question: Work performance data collected during execution includes:
options: A. Only financial metrics
B. Raw observations and measurements about activity status
C. The project charter
D. Lessons learned from past projects
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, work performance data consists of raw observations and measurements gathered during execution, such as percent complete, actual start/finish dates, actual costs, defect counts, and hours worked.

questions.question: A corrective action is taken to:
options: A. Prevent potential future problems
B. Bring expected future project performance in line with the plan
C. Celebrate project milestones
D. Add new features to the project
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, corrective actions realign expected future performance with the project management plan. Preventive actions reduce the probability of potential future deviations. Defect repairs fix identified non-conformities.

questions.question: Variance analysis compares:
options: A. Different project methodologies
B. Actual project performance against the baseline
C. Team member salaries
D. Vendor proposals
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, variance analysis compares actual performance to the planned baseline for scope, schedule, and cost. Variances indicate where the project is deviating from the plan and may require corrective action.

questions.question: A project has a Schedule Performance Index (SPI) of 0.85. This means:
options: A. The project is ahead of schedule
B. The project is behind schedule, completing only 85% of planned work
C. The project is exactly on schedule
D. The schedule cannot be measured
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, SPI = EV/PV. An SPI of 0.85 means the project is only completing 85 cents of planned work for every dollar of planned value. SPI < 1.0 indicates behind schedule; SPI > 1.0 indicates ahead of schedule.

questions.question: A CPI of 1.15 indicates the project is:
options: A. Over budget by 15%
B. Under budget, getting $1.15 of value for every $1 spent
C. Behind schedule by 15%
D. Exactly on budget
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, CPI = EV/AC. A CPI of 1.15 means the project is earning $1.15 of value for every $1.00 spent — it is under budget. CPI > 1.0 is favorable; CPI < 1.0 indicates over budget.

questions.question: Scope validation involves:
options: A. The PM inspecting deliverables for quality
B. The customer formally accepting completed deliverables
C. Updating the risk register
D. Creating the WBS
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, scope validation (verification) is the process of formalizing acceptance of completed deliverables with the customer or sponsor. It confirms deliverables meet the acceptance criteria defined in the scope baseline.

questions.question: Estimate at Completion (EAC) represents:
options: A. The original project budget
B. The expected total cost of the project based on current performance
C. The amount of work remaining
D. The actual cost spent to date
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, EAC is the expected total cost of completing all project work. A common formula is EAC = BAC / CPI, which projects the final cost based on current cost performance. It helps stakeholders understand the likely final budget.

questions.question: During project closure, lessons learned are documented to:
options: A. Assign blame for project failures
B. Capture knowledge for future projects and organizational improvement
C. Justify additional budget requests
D. Extend the project timeline
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.6, lessons learned capture what went well, what went poorly, and what should be done differently. They become organizational process assets that benefit future projects and contribute to continuous improvement.

questions.question: Administrative closure includes all of the following EXCEPT:
options: A. Archiving project documents
B. Releasing project resources
C. Creating the project charter
D. Obtaining final acceptance
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.6, administrative closure includes obtaining final acceptance, archiving documents, releasing resources, closing contracts, updating organizational process assets, and conducting post-project reviews. The charter is created during initiation.

questions.question: Which of the following occur during the closing phase? (Select THREE)
options: A. Final deliverable acceptance
B. Sprint planning
C. Lessons learned documentation
D. Release of project resources
E. Creating the WBS
F. Feasibility study
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.6, closing phase activities include final acceptance, lessons learned, resource release, contract closure, document archiving, final reports, and knowledge transfer. Sprint planning, WBS, and feasibility studies occur in earlier phases.

questions.question: Knowledge transfer during project closure ensures:
options: A. The project manager retains exclusive knowledge
B. The operations team can support and maintain the deliverables
C. No documentation is needed
D. The project can be restarted at any time
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.6, knowledge transfer ensures that the operations and support teams have all the information needed to maintain, support, and operate the project deliverables after the project team disbands.

questions.question: A post-implementation review is conducted to:
options: A. Approve the project charter
B. Evaluate whether the project achieved its intended business objectives
C. Create the risk register
D. Assign resources to the next project
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.6, a post-implementation review (conducted weeks or months after closure) evaluates whether the project delivered the expected business value and achieved the objectives stated in the business case.

questions.question: A network diagram using the Precedence Diagramming Method (PDM) shows:
options: A. Team member reporting relationships
B. Activity dependencies using nodes and arrows
C. Project budget allocation
D. Stakeholder communication preferences
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, PDM (Activity-on-Node) network diagrams represent activities as nodes connected by arrows showing dependencies. They are used to visualize the sequence of activities and identify the critical path.

questions.question: A project dashboard provides:
options: A. Detailed source code listings
B. A high-level visual summary of project health and key metrics
C. Team member vacation schedules
D. Vendor contract details
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a project dashboard provides an at-a-glance visual summary of project status including KPIs, schedule status, budget health, risk indicators, and milestone progress using charts and indicators (red/yellow/green).

questions.question: A histogram in project management is commonly used to:
options: A. Show the critical path
B. Display resource allocation over time
C. Document lessons learned
D. Track stakeholder engagement
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a resource histogram shows resource allocation (typically staffing levels) over time using bar charts. It helps identify periods of over- or under-allocation and supports resource leveling decisions.

questions.question: A burnup chart differs from a burndown chart in that a burnup chart shows:
options: A. Only negative trends
B. Cumulative work completed and total scope over time
C. The project budget burn rate
D. Team morale over time
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a burnup chart shows two lines: cumulative work completed (trending up) and total scope. It clearly shows scope changes — if the total scope line rises, scope was added. Burndown charts only show remaining work.

questions.question: A scatter diagram is used to:
options: A. Show the relationship between two variables
B. Display the project schedule
C. Track issue resolution
D. Assign team roles
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a scatter diagram (scatter plot) plots two variables on X and Y axes to show correlation patterns. It helps determine if a relationship exists between variables, such as hours of testing vs. defects found.

questions.question: A flowchart in project management is used to:
options: A. Calculate earned value metrics
B. Display a process or workflow showing steps, decisions, and outcomes
C. Track team member hours
D. Plan the project budget
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, flowcharts visually represent processes showing steps, decision points (diamonds), inputs, outputs, and flow direction. They help understand, analyze, and improve processes.

questions.question: An affinity diagram is used to:
options: A. Calculate project costs
B. Group ideas or data into categories based on natural relationships
C. Schedule project activities
D. Measure quality defects
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, an affinity diagram organizes large amounts of ideas, data, or issues into groups based on natural relationships or themes. It is often used after brainstorming sessions to categorize and prioritize ideas.

questions.question: Which of the following are Agile-specific project management tools? (Select TWO)
options: A. Burndown chart
B. PERT chart
C. Kanban board
D. Gantt chart
E. Earned value report
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, burndown charts and Kanban boards are Agile-specific tools. PERT charts, Gantt charts, and earned value reports are traditional/predictive project management tools.

questions.question: A velocity chart shows:
options: A. How fast team members type
B. The amount of work completed per sprint over multiple sprints
C. Network traffic speed
D. The critical path duration
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a velocity chart tracks the amount of work (story points) completed per sprint across multiple sprints. It shows trends in team productivity and helps forecast future sprint capacity.

questions.question: The communication plan defines:
options: A. The project's technical architecture
B. What information will be communicated, to whom, how, and when
C. The project budget breakdown
D. Team member job descriptions
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, the communication plan defines what information will be distributed, who receives it, the method of delivery, frequency, format, and responsible party. It ensures stakeholders receive the right information at the right time.

questions.question: A change log records:
options: A. Only approved changes
B. All change requests and their current status (pending, approved, rejected)
C. Team member attendance
D. Budget expenditures only
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, the change log documents all change requests submitted during the project, including their description, date, requestor, status (pending/approved/rejected/deferred), and disposition.

questions.question: A Statement of Work (SOW) describes:
options: A. The project manager's authority level
B. The specific work to be performed under a contract, including deliverables and timeline
C. The team's daily standup agenda
D. The organization's strategic plan
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, the SOW is a narrative description of the products, services, or results to be provided under a contract. It includes scope of work, deliverables, schedule, acceptance criteria, and performance standards.

questions.question: Meeting minutes should include:
options: A. Only the project manager's opinions
B. Key decisions, action items, owners, and due dates
C. Verbatim transcripts of all conversations
D. Team member performance ratings
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, meeting minutes document key discussion points, decisions made, action items with assigned owners and due dates, attendees, and any follow-up needed. They provide an official record of the meeting.

questions.question: A project closure report typically includes:
options: A. Sprint backlog items for the next project
B. Summary of project performance, lessons learned, and final deliverable status
C. Detailed source code documentation
D. Vendor marketing materials
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, the project closure report summarizes overall project performance (scope, schedule, budget, quality), lessons learned, final deliverable status, outstanding issues, and recommendations for future projects.

questions.question: Which of the following are procurement documents? (Select TWO)
options: A. Request for Proposal (RFP)
B. Burndown chart
C. Statement of Work (SOW)
D. Daily standup notes
E. Velocity chart
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, procurement documents include RFI (Request for Information), RFP (Request for Proposal), RFQ (Request for Quote), SOW (Statement of Work), and contracts. Burndown charts and velocity charts are Agile tools.

questions.question: Schedule Variance (SV) is calculated as:
options: A. SV = AC - PV
B. SV = EV - PV
C. SV = EV - AC
D. SV = PV - AC
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, Schedule Variance = Earned Value - Planned Value (SV = EV - PV). A negative SV indicates the project is behind schedule. A positive SV means ahead of schedule.

questions.question: Cost Variance (CV) is calculated as:
options: A. CV = PV - AC
B. CV = AC - EV
C. CV = EV - AC
D. CV = PV - EV
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, Cost Variance = Earned Value - Actual Cost (CV = EV - AC). A negative CV indicates over budget. A positive CV means under budget. For example, if EV=$80K and AC=$90K, CV = -$10K (over budget).

questions.question: A project has BAC=$200,000, EV=$100,000, AC=$120,000, PV=$110,000. The CPI is:
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, CPI = EV/AC = $100,000/$120,000 = 0.83. This means for every dollar spent, only $0.83 of value was earned. The project is over budget.

questions.question: Using the same project data (BAC=$200K, EV=$100K, AC=$120K), the EAC using CPI is:
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, EAC = BAC/CPI = $200,000/0.83 = $240,964. This forecasts the total project cost if current cost performance continues. The project is expected to be approximately $41K over the original budget.

questions.question: Estimate to Complete (ETC) represents:
options: A. The total project budget
B. The expected cost to finish the remaining project work
C. The actual cost spent so far
D. The planned value of all work
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, ETC = EAC - AC. It represents the expected cost to complete the remaining work. If EAC=$240K and AC=$120K, then ETC=$120K more is needed to finish the project.

questions.question: Variance at Completion (VAC) tells the project manager:
options: A. How many resources are available
B. The expected budget surplus or deficit at project completion
C. The current schedule status
D. How many risks have been identified
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, VAC = BAC - EAC. It shows the expected budget variance at completion. A negative VAC indicates the project will finish over budget. If BAC=$200K and EAC=$240K, VAC = -$40K (over budget by $40K).

questions.question: Planned Value (PV) represents:
options: A. The actual cost of work performed
B. The authorized budget assigned to scheduled work
C. The value of completed work
D. The total project budget
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, Planned Value (PV) is the authorized budget for the work scheduled to be completed by a given date. It represents what should have been accomplished according to the plan.

questions.question: Earned Value (EV) represents:
options: A. The amount invoiced to the client
B. The value of the work actually completed, measured against the budget
C. The actual cost of resources used
D. The profit earned by the project
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, Earned Value (EV) is the measure of work performed expressed in terms of the budget authorized for that work. It represents how much of the planned budget has been earned by completing work.

questions.question: A project has EV=$50K and PV=$60K. The SPI is:
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, SPI = EV/PV = $50,000/$60,000 = 0.83. The project is behind schedule — only 83% of the planned work has been completed. The team needs to accelerate or adjust the schedule.

questions.question: Budget at Completion (BAC) represents:
options: A. The actual total cost at the end of the project
B. The total approved budget for the project
C. The cost of the next phase only
D. The vendor's contract value
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, BAC is the total approved budget for the project — the sum of all planned values. It serves as the baseline against which actual performance is measured throughout the project.

questions.question: Which of the following indicate a project is in trouble? (Select TWO)
options: A. CPI of 1.15
B. SPI of 0.75
E. CPI of 1.00
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, SPI of 0.75 means only 75% of planned work is done (behind schedule). CV of -$50K means the project is $50K over budget. CPI of 1.15 and SV of $10K are favorable. CPI of 1.00 means exactly on budget.

questions.question: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) provides:
options: A. Fully managed applications
B. Virtualized computing resources like servers, storage, and networking
C. Only email services
D. Pre-built software platforms for development
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, IaaS provides virtualized computing infrastructure (servers, storage, networking) over the cloud. The customer manages the OS, applications, and data, while the provider manages the physical infrastructure.

questions.question: Platform as a Service (PaaS) is BEST suited for:
options: A. End users accessing email and productivity apps
B. Developers building and deploying applications without managing infrastructure
C. Network administrators configuring firewalls
D. Data center technicians maintaining servers
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, PaaS provides a platform for developers to build, test, and deploy applications without managing the underlying infrastructure. Examples include AWS Elastic Beanstalk, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure App Service.

questions.question: A hybrid cloud combines:
options: A. Only public cloud services from multiple providers
B. Public and private cloud environments with data sharing between them
C. Only on-premises infrastructure
D. Cloud and manual paper-based systems
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, a hybrid cloud combines public cloud, private cloud, and/or on-premises infrastructure, allowing data and applications to move between environments. It provides flexibility, security, and cost optimization.

questions.question: DevOps is BEST described as:
options: A. A software programming language
B. A culture and set of practices that unify software development and IT operations
C. A type of cloud service
D. A project management methodology
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, DevOps combines development (Dev) and operations (Ops) practices to shorten the development lifecycle and deliver high-quality software continuously. Key practices include CI/CD, automation, monitoring, and collaboration.

questions.question: Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) automates:
options: A. Team member scheduling
B. Building, testing, and deploying code changes
C. Project budgeting
D. Stakeholder communication
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, CI/CD is a DevOps practice that automates building, testing, and deploying code changes. CI merges code changes frequently with automated testing; CD automatically deploys tested code to production.

questions.question: A VPN (Virtual Private Network) is used to:
options: A. Increase internet speed
B. Create a secure, encrypted connection over a public network
C. Replace the need for antivirus software
D. Store files in the cloud
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, a VPN creates an encrypted tunnel over a public network (internet) to securely connect remote users or sites to a private network. It protects data in transit from eavesdropping.

questions.question: A disaster recovery plan (DRP) differs from a business continuity plan (BCP) in that a DRP:
options: A. Is only needed for natural disasters
B. Focuses specifically on restoring IT systems and data after a disruption
C. Replaces the need for data backups
D. Is the same as a project management plan
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, a DRP focuses on restoring IT infrastructure, systems, and data after a disaster. A BCP is broader, covering all business functions to maintain operations during and after a disruption.

questions.question: An API (Application Programming Interface) allows:
options: A. Users to access the internet
B. Different software applications to communicate with each other
C. Hardware components to be physically connected
D. Project managers to create Gantt charts
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, an API defines how software components interact, allowing applications to exchange data and functionality. APIs enable integration between systems, microservices architecture, and third-party service consumption.

questions.question: Which of the following are cloud deployment models? (Select THREE)
options: A. Public cloud
B. Agile cloud
C. Private cloud
D. Hybrid cloud
E. Waterfall cloud
F. Kanban cloud
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, the three main cloud deployment models are public (shared infrastructure), private (dedicated infrastructure), and hybrid (combination). Community cloud is a fourth model. Agile, Waterfall, and Kanban are methodologies, not cloud models.

questions.question: Version control (source control) systems are used to:
options: A. Track project budgets
B. Track and manage changes to code, documents, or files over time
C. Schedule team meetings
D. Monitor network performance
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, version control systems (like Git) track changes to files over time, enabling teams to collaborate, review history, revert to previous versions, and manage concurrent modifications through branching and merging.

questions.question: Scalability in IT refers to:
options: A. The physical size of server hardware
B. A system's ability to handle increased workload by adding resources
C. The number of team members on a project
D. The speed of network connections
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, scalability is the ability of a system to handle growing workloads by adding resources. Horizontal scaling adds more machines; vertical scaling adds more power to existing machines. Cloud computing enables elastic scaling.

questions.question: The Agile Manifesto was created to address problems with:
options: A. Cloud computing infrastructure
B. Heavyweight, documentation-driven software development processes
C. Team member compensation
D. Hardware manufacturing
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, the Agile Manifesto (2001) was created by 17 software developers who recognized that traditional heavyweight processes were too rigid and documentation-heavy. They proposed values emphasizing flexibility, collaboration, and working software.

questions.question: Story points in Agile measure:
options: A. The exact hours needed to complete a user story
B. The relative effort, complexity, and uncertainty of a user story
C. The number of lines of code
D. The cost of development
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, story points are a relative measure of effort, complexity, and uncertainty involved in completing a user story. They allow teams to estimate work without committing to exact hours, using techniques like planning poker.

questions.question: Planning poker is an Agile estimation technique where:
options: A. Team members play cards for fun during breaks
B. Team members simultaneously reveal their estimates to avoid anchoring bias
C. The project manager assigns estimates to each task
D. Only the Scrum Master provides estimates
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, planning poker has team members independently select cards representing their story point estimates, then reveal simultaneously. This prevents anchoring bias and promotes discussion when estimates differ significantly.

questions.question: A Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is:
options: A. A product with no features
B. The simplest version of a product that delivers value and enables learning
C. The final, feature-complete product
D. A product that fails quality testing
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, an MVP is the simplest version of a product that delivers enough value to early users and enables learning about customer needs with minimal effort. It validates assumptions and guides future development.

questions.question: Product backlog refinement (grooming) involves:
options: A. Deleting all items from the backlog
B. Reviewing, updating, and adding detail to product backlog items
C. Closing the project
D. Conducting performance reviews
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, backlog refinement is an ongoing activity where the team reviews product backlog items, adds details, re-estimates, and re-prioritizes. It ensures upcoming sprint items are well-understood and ready for sprint planning.

questions.question: An epic in Agile is:
options: A. A very small task that takes less than an hour
B. A large body of work that can be broken down into smaller user stories
C. A type of sprint
D. The same as a bug report
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, an epic is a large user story that is too big to complete in a single sprint. It is broken down into smaller, more manageable user stories. Epics help organize and group related features at a higher level.

questions.question: Acceptance criteria for a user story define:
options: A. The salary requirements for team members
B. The conditions that must be met for the story to be considered complete
C. The project sponsor's expectations for ROI
D. The number of sprints needed
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, acceptance criteria are specific conditions that must be satisfied for a user story to be considered done. They are testable, clear, and agreed upon by the team and Product Owner before development begins.

questions.question: GDPR primarily protects:
options: A. Financial transaction data in the US
B. Personal data of individuals in the European Union
C. Intellectual property of software companies
D. Medical records in Canada
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) protects the personal data and privacy of individuals in the EU. It requires organizations to handle personal data responsibly, provide consent mechanisms, and enable data deletion rights.

questions.question: PCI-DSS applies to organizations that:
options: A. Develop mobile applications
B. Process, store, or transmit credit card data
C. Manage government contracts
D. Provide healthcare services
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, PCI-DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) establishes security requirements for organizations that process, store, or transmit cardholder data. Non-compliance can result in fines and loss of card processing privileges.

questions.question: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) primarily affects:
options: A. Healthcare organizations
B. Publicly traded companies' financial reporting and internal controls
C. Social media companies
D. Non-profit organizations
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, SOX requires publicly traded companies to maintain accurate financial records and implement internal controls to prevent fraud. IT projects at these companies must ensure compliance with SOX requirements for data integrity.

questions.question: Data sovereignty refers to:
options: A. The organization's right to delete any data
B. Data being subject to the laws of the country where it is stored
C. The team's ownership of project documentation
D. The sponsor's authority over project data
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, data sovereignty means data is subject to the laws and governance of the nation where it is physically stored. This impacts cloud computing decisions — data stored in the EU falls under GDPR regardless of where the company is headquartered.

questions.question: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) includes:
options: A. Only social security numbers
B. Any data that can identify a specific individual, such as name, email, or SSN
C. Only medical records
D. Public company financial statements
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, PII is any information that can be used to identify a specific individual, including name, address, email, phone number, SSN, biometric data, and date of birth. Projects handling PII must implement appropriate safeguards.

questions.question: Which of the following are regulatory frameworks that may impact IT projects? (Select TWO)
options: A. HIPAA
B. Scrum Guide
C. GDPR
D. Agile Manifesto
E. Kanban Method
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, HIPAA and GDPR are regulatory frameworks that impose compliance requirements on projects handling health data and EU personal data respectively. Scrum Guide, Agile Manifesto, and Kanban Method are development frameworks.

questions.question: Privacy by design means:
options: A. Adding privacy features after the product launches
B. Integrating privacy protections into the system from the beginning of development
C. Hiding all project documentation from stakeholders
D. Encrypting only the database
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, privacy by design embeds privacy considerations into every stage of development — from requirements through design, implementation, and deployment. It is proactive rather than reactive and is required by regulations like GDPR.

questions.question: ITIL is BEST described as:
options: A. A programming language
B. A framework for IT service management best practices
C. A type of cloud service
D. An Agile methodology
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, ITIL (Information Technology Infrastructure Library) is a set of best practices for IT service management (ITSM). It covers service strategy, design, transition, operation, and continual improvement.

questions.question: A Change Advisory Board (CAB) in IT governance:
options: A. Only manages project budgets
B. Reviews and approves changes to IT systems to minimize risk
C. Writes software code
D. Conducts employee performance reviews
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, a CAB reviews proposed changes to IT systems, assesses risk, and recommends approval, rejection, or modification. It ensures changes are properly planned, tested, and communicated to minimize service disruption.

questions.question: Separation of duties is a governance control that:
options: A. Ensures all team members work in separate offices
B. Divides critical tasks among multiple people to prevent fraud or errors
C. Separates the development and testing teams geographically
D. Keeps project documentation in separate folders
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, separation of duties divides critical functions among different people so no single person has complete control over a process. For example, the person who writes code should not be the same person who approves it for production.

questions.question: The principle of least privilege states that:
options: A. All team members should have administrator access
B. Users should have only the minimum access needed to perform their job
C. Project managers should have less authority than functional managers
D. Budget should be minimized for all projects
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, least privilege is a security principle granting users only the minimum permissions needed to perform their duties. This limits the potential damage from accidental or malicious actions and reduces security risk.

questions.question: Organizational change management (OCM) focuses on:
options: A. Managing source code changes
B. Helping people adopt new processes, tools, or organizational structures
C. Tracking budget changes
D. Modifying the project schedule
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, OCM focuses on the people side of change — helping employees adapt to new processes, technology, or structures. It includes communication, training, stakeholder engagement, and resistance management.

questions.question: Data governance ensures:
options: A. All data is deleted after the project ends
B. Data is properly managed, secured, and used according to policies and regulations
C. Only the DBA can access any data
D. Data is never shared between departments
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, data governance establishes policies, procedures, and standards for managing data assets. It covers data quality, security, privacy, lifecycle management, and compliance with regulations.

questions.question: Which of the following are IT governance frameworks? (Select TWO)
options: A. COBIT
B. Scrum
C. ITIL
D. Kanban
E. Extreme Programming
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, COBIT (Control Objectives for Information and Related Technologies) and ITIL are IT governance frameworks. Scrum, Kanban, and XP are Agile development frameworks, not governance frameworks.

questions.question: Benefits realization management ensures:
options: A. All team members receive bonuses
B. The project delivers the intended business value and benefits
C. The project stays under budget
D. Vendors are paid on time
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, benefits realization management tracks and ensures that the expected benefits defined in the business case are actually achieved. It extends beyond project closure to verify that outcomes match the investment justification.

questions.question: An Agile principle states that the best architectures, requirements, and designs emerge from:
options: A. Senior management directives
B. Self-organizing teams
C. External consultants
D. Waterfall documentation
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, one of the 12 Agile principles states that the best architectures, requirements, and designs emerge from self-organizing teams. This empowers teams to make technical decisions and fosters innovation.

questions.question: T-shirt sizing in Agile estimation uses:
options: A. Exact hour estimates
B. Relative sizes like XS, S, M, L, XL for quick high-level estimation
C. Dollar amounts
D. Fibonacci numbers only
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, T-shirt sizing is a quick, high-level estimation technique using relative sizes (XS, S, M, L, XL). It is useful for initial backlog prioritization when detailed estimates are not yet needed.

questions.question: Scope verification ensures that:
options: A. The project scope has not changed since initiation
B. Completed deliverables are formally accepted by the customer
C. All risks have been mitigated
D. The budget has not been exceeded
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.3, scope verification (validation) is the formal acceptance of completed deliverables by the customer or sponsor. It confirms deliverables meet acceptance criteria and closes out work packages.

questions.question: Risk sharing is a positive risk response strategy where:
options: A. The risk is transferred to a third party
B. The opportunity is allocated to a third party best able to capture it
C. The team ignores the risk
D. The risk is eliminated entirely
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, sharing allocates a positive risk (opportunity) to a third party that is better positioned to capture it. For example, forming a joint venture to pursue a market opportunity that neither party could capture alone.

questions.question: A secondary risk is:
options: A. A risk that is less important than the primary risk
B. A new risk that arises as a result of implementing a risk response
C. A risk identified during project closure
D. A risk that has been accepted
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, a secondary risk is a new risk created by implementing a risk response strategy. For example, hiring a subcontractor (risk mitigation) introduces a new risk of subcontractor performance issues.

questions.question: A workaround is:
options: A. A pre-planned risk response
B. An unplanned response to a risk that has occurred without a planned response
C. A permanent fix for a known issue
D. An alternative project methodology
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, a workaround is an unplanned response to an unidentified risk or a risk that was accepted but has now occurred. Unlike contingency plans, workarounds are created reactively when unexpected events happen.

questions.question: The forward pass in CPM calculates:
options: A. The latest possible start and finish dates
B. The earliest possible start and finish dates
C. The project budget
D. Resource requirements
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, the forward pass calculates the early start (ES) and early finish (EF) dates for each activity by moving forward through the network diagram. The backward pass calculates late start (LS) and late finish (LF).

questions.question: Resource smoothing adjusts activities within their float to:
options: A. Extend the project deadline
B. Optimize resource usage without changing the critical path
C. Add more resources to the project
D. Remove non-essential activities
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, resource smoothing adjusts activities within their available float to reduce resource peaks without extending the project end date. Unlike resource leveling, it does not allow the critical path to change.

questions.question: Parametric estimating uses:
options: A. Expert judgment from similar projects
B. Statistical relationships between historical data and project variables
C. A single point estimate from the sponsor
D. Random number generation
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, parametric estimating uses statistical relationships between historical data and project variables. For example, cost per square foot × total square footage, or hours per line of code × estimated lines.

questions.question: Six Sigma aims to:
options: A. Increase project scope
B. Reduce defects to fewer than 3.4 per million opportunities
C. Eliminate all project risks
D. Shorten the project schedule by 50%
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.7, Six Sigma is a data-driven quality methodology that targets reducing defects to 3.4 per million opportunities. It uses DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control) for process improvement.

questions.question: Kaizen is a quality concept that emphasizes:
options: A. Radical one-time changes
B. Continuous, incremental improvement
C. Eliminating all testing phases
D. Outsourcing quality assurance
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.7, Kaizen is a Japanese philosophy meaning 'change for better' that emphasizes continuous, small, incremental improvements involving all team members. It is a core principle of Lean and Total Quality Management.

questions.question: An information radiator is:
options: A. A heating device in the server room
B. A highly visible display of project information like Kanban boards or burndown charts
C. A type of email filter
D. A stakeholder communication report
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.8, an information radiator is a large, highly visible display (physical or digital) that shows project information at a glance. Examples include Kanban boards, burndown charts, and dashboards displayed on monitors.

questions.question: A project has 10 stakeholders. A new team member joins. How many additional communication channels are created?
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.8, with 10 stakeholders: 10(9)/2 = 45 channels. With 11: 11(10)/2 = 55 channels. The difference is 55 - 45 = 10 new channels. Each new person adds (n) channels where n is the previous number of people.

questions.question: Effective meeting management requires all of the following EXCEPT:
options: A. A published agenda distributed in advance
B. A designated timekeeper
C. Allowing unlimited discussion without focus
D. Documented action items with owners and due dates
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.9, effective meetings require published agendas, timekeepers, focused discussions, documented decisions and action items, and follow-up. Unlimited unfocused discussion wastes time and reduces meeting effectiveness.

questions.question: According to Maslow's hierarchy, once physiological and safety needs are met, people seek:
options: A. Financial compensation
B. Social belonging and esteem
C. Longer working hours
D. More project constraints
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, Maslow's hierarchy progresses: physiological, safety, social belonging, esteem, and self-actualization. Project managers can motivate teams by understanding and addressing needs at the appropriate level.

questions.question: Herzberg's hygiene factors include:
options: A. Achievement and recognition
B. Salary, working conditions, and company policies
C. Creativity and innovation
D. Self-actualization and growth
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, Herzberg's two-factor theory distinguishes between hygiene factors (salary, conditions, policies — their absence causes dissatisfaction) and motivators (achievement, recognition, growth — their presence drives satisfaction).

questions.question: A PM uses their personal charisma and the respect of team members to influence decisions. This is an example of:
options: A. Legitimate power
B. Coercive power
C. Referent power
D. Reward power
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, referent power is based on the leader's personal charisma, trustworthiness, and the respect they command. People follow because they admire and want to be like the leader.

questions.question: During the storming phase of team development, the PM should:
options: A. Ignore conflicts and focus only on deliverables
B. Facilitate conflict resolution and help establish team norms
C. Disband the team and form a new one
D. Escalate all conflicts to the sponsor
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, during storming, conflicts arise as team members assert their ideas and compete for influence. The PM should facilitate resolution, establish ground rules, clarify roles, and guide the team toward norming.

questions.question: Compromising as a conflict resolution technique:
options: A. Produces a win-win solution for all parties
B. Provides a solution where each party gives up something
C. Forces one party to accept the other's position
D. Ignores the conflict entirely
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, compromise is a lose-lose approach where each party makes concessions. Unlike collaboration (win-win), neither side is fully satisfied. It is useful when time is limited and a quick resolution is needed.

questions.question: Emotional intelligence in project management includes:
options: A. Only technical knowledge
B. Self-awareness, empathy, social skills, and self-regulation
C. Budget management skills
D. Scheduling expertise
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, emotional intelligence includes self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, and social skills. PMs with high EQ build better relationships, manage conflicts effectively, and lead teams more successfully.

questions.question: A cost-reimbursable contract puts MORE financial risk on:
options: A. The seller/vendor
B. The buyer
C. The project sponsor
D. The end user
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.11, in a cost-reimbursable contract, the buyer pays the seller's actual costs plus a fee. The buyer bears the financial risk because costs can exceed initial estimates. Fixed-price contracts shift risk to the seller.

questions.question: A Service Level Agreement (SLA) defines:
options: A. The project team's working hours
B. Expected performance standards and metrics between service provider and customer
C. The project charter content
D. Team member job descriptions
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.11, an SLA defines the level of service expected from a provider, including performance metrics (uptime, response time), responsibilities, penalties for non-compliance, and measurement methods.

questions.question: A benefit-cost ratio greater than 1.0 indicates:
options: A. The project costs more than its benefits
B. The project benefits exceed its costs
C. The project should be cancelled
D. The project is exactly on budget
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.1, a benefit-cost ratio (BCR) greater than 1.0 means benefits exceed costs, indicating a worthwhile investment. A BCR of 1.5 means $1.50 in benefits for every $1.00 spent. Higher ratios are more attractive.

questions.question: Internal Rate of Return (IRR) is:
options: A. The interest rate on the project's bank loan
B. The discount rate that makes the NPV of a project equal to zero
C. The project's profit margin
D. The rate of team member turnover
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.1, IRR is the discount rate at which a project's NPV equals zero. Projects with an IRR exceeding the organization's required rate of return are generally considered worthwhile investments.

questions.question: Enterprise Environmental Factors (EEFs) that influence projects include:
options: A. Only internal company policies
B. Market conditions, regulations, organizational culture, and industry standards
C. The project management plan
D. Lessons learned from past projects
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.2, EEFs are conditions not under the project team's control that influence the project, including market conditions, government regulations, organizational culture, political climate, and industry standards.

questions.question: Organizational Process Assets (OPAs) include:
options: A. Only the organization's physical assets
B. Templates, procedures, lessons learned, and historical information
C. Team member personal files
D. Vendor marketing materials
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.2, OPAs are plans, processes, policies, procedures, templates, and knowledge bases (like lessons learned) from the performing organization. They provide guidance and historical reference for project teams.

questions.question: The change management plan describes:
options: A. How team members will relocate offices
B. How changes to the project will be formally managed, approved, and documented
C. How the product will be marketed
D. How stakeholders will be identified
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, the change management plan defines how changes to the project scope, schedule, cost, and deliverables will be requested, reviewed, approved, implemented, and documented throughout the project lifecycle.

questions.question: A resource breakdown structure (RBS) organizes:
options: A. Project deliverables into work packages
B. Project resources by category and type in a hierarchical format
C. Stakeholders by influence level
D. Risks by probability
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, the RBS is a hierarchical representation of resources organized by category (labor, materials, equipment) and type. It helps ensure all needed resources are identified and planned for.

questions.question: Which of the following are risk identification techniques? (Select THREE)
options: A. Brainstorming
B. Resource leveling
C. Delphi technique
D. Fast tracking
E. SWOT analysis
F. Crashing
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, risk identification techniques include brainstorming, Delphi technique, SWOT analysis, interviews, checklists, and document review. Resource leveling, fast tracking, and crashing are scheduling techniques.

questions.question: The Delphi technique for risk identification involves:
options: A. Assigning risks to the lowest-level team member
B. Anonymous expert input gathered iteratively until consensus is reached
C. Using Monte Carlo simulation
D. Reviewing only the risk register from the previous project
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, the Delphi technique gathers anonymous expert opinions through multiple rounds of questionnaires. After each round, a summary is shared and experts can revise their input until the group converges on consensus.

questions.question: Managing stakeholder engagement during execution involves:
options: A. Ignoring stakeholders until the project is complete
B. Communicating with stakeholders, addressing their concerns, and maintaining relationships
C. Only reporting to the project sponsor
D. Sending one status report at the end of the project
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, managing stakeholder engagement means proactively communicating with stakeholders, addressing their needs and concerns, resolving issues, managing expectations, and fostering supportive relationships throughout execution.

questions.question: A quality audit during execution examines:
options: A. Only the final deliverable
B. Whether project activities comply with organizational and project policies and processes
C. Team member attendance records
D. The project charter approval
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, a quality audit is a structured, independent review that determines whether project activities comply with organizational and project policies, processes, and procedures. It identifies best practices and areas for improvement.

questions.question: Virtual team management requires additional focus on:
options: A. Reducing all communication to email only
B. Clear communication, trust building, and technology-enabled collaboration
C. Requiring all team members to relocate to one office
D. Eliminating all meetings
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, virtual teams need clear communication protocols, trust-building activities, reliable collaboration tools, sensitivity to time zones and cultural differences, and more frequent check-ins to maintain team cohesion.

questions.question: Work performance information is created by:
options: A. The project sponsor alone
B. Analyzing and interpreting work performance data in context
C. Ignoring actual project results
D. Copying the project management plan
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, work performance information is the analyzed and contextualized version of raw work performance data. For example, SPI/CPI calculations, variance analysis results, and trend assessments are work performance information.

questions.question: A trend analysis looks at:
options: A. A single data point in time
B. Project performance over time to identify patterns and forecast future results
C. Only the project budget
D. Team member satisfaction scores
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, trend analysis examines project performance results over time to determine if performance is improving or deteriorating. It helps forecast future performance and identify when corrective action is needed.

questions.question: Contract closure involves:
options: A. Only paying the vendor
B. Verifying all contract deliverables are complete, resolving disputes, and formally closing the contract
C. Starting a new contract
D. Extending the contract indefinitely
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.6, contract closure verifies all contractual deliverables are complete and accepted, resolves any open claims or disputes, processes final payments, and formally closes the procurement record.

questions.question: A project that is part of a larger program should align with:
options: A. Individual team member goals
B. The program's strategic objectives and benefits
C. Competing project budgets
D. The vendor's business plan
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.1, projects within a program are managed coordinately to achieve program-level strategic benefits. Each project contributes to the overall program objectives and must align with the program's goals.

questions.question: A requirements document should include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: A. Functional requirements
B. Non-functional requirements
C. Acceptance criteria
D. Team member salary information
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.3, requirements documents capture functional requirements (what the system does), non-functional requirements (performance, security, usability), and acceptance criteria. Personnel compensation is not a project requirement.

questions.question: A risk owner is the person who:
options: A. Identified the risk first
B. Is assigned to monitor and manage a specific risk and its response
C. Caused the risk to occur
D. Has the largest budget on the project
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, a risk owner is the individual assigned responsibility for monitoring a specific risk, implementing the risk response strategy, and reporting on its status. Every identified risk should have an assigned owner.

questions.question: Passive acceptance of a risk means:
options: A. Developing a detailed contingency plan
B. Acknowledging the risk but not taking proactive action unless it occurs
C. Transferring the risk to insurance
D. Eliminating the risk from the project
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, passive acceptance acknowledges the risk without developing a contingency plan. The team will deal with the risk if and when it occurs. Active acceptance involves creating contingency reserves or plans.

questions.question: Total Quality Management (TQM) emphasizes:
options: A. Only final product inspection
B. Organization-wide commitment to quality involving all employees
C. Quality management by external auditors only
D. Reducing quality to cut costs
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.7, TQM is an approach where all members of the organization participate in improving processes, products, services, and culture. It focuses on long-term success through customer satisfaction and continuous improvement.

questions.question: A quality baseline defines:
options: A. The minimum acceptable budget for quality activities
B. The quality objectives and acceptable thresholds for the project
C. The number of quality auditors needed
D. The testing schedule
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.7, the quality baseline documents the quality objectives of the project and defines the acceptable quality thresholds and metrics. It is used as a reference to measure and report quality performance.

questions.question: A salience model classifies stakeholders based on:
options: A. Their salary and job title
B. Power, legitimacy, and urgency
C. Geographic location only
D. Technical skills and experience
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.2, the salience model classifies stakeholders using three dimensions: power (ability to influence), legitimacy (appropriateness of involvement), and urgency (need for immediate attention). Stakeholders with all three are definitive.

questions.question: A RACI chart shows 'Accountable' for a task means:
options: A. The person does the work
B. The one person ultimately answerable for the correct completion of the task
C. A person who gives input before the decision
D. A person who is kept up to date on progress
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, in a RACI matrix, Accountable means the one person who is ultimately answerable for the task's correct completion. There should be exactly one 'A' per task. Responsible does the work, Consulted provides input, Informed receives updates.

questions.question: A preventive action is taken to:
options: A. Fix a defect that has already occurred
B. Reduce the probability of a negative consequence in the future
C. Celebrate a project milestone
D. Add new features to the deliverable
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, preventive actions are taken to reduce the probability or impact of potential future problems. They are proactive, unlike corrective actions which are reactive responses to existing deviations.

questions.question: During execution, the PM discovers that two team members have conflicting work styles. The PM should:
options: A. Immediately transfer one team member
B. Address the conflict early through facilitation and establish clear working agreements
C. Wait for the conflict to resolve itself
D. Report both team members to HR
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, the PM should address team conflicts early before they escalate. Facilitated discussions help team members understand different perspectives, establish working agreements, and find collaborative solutions.

questions.question: A change request can result from all of the following EXCEPT:
options: A. A defect found during quality control
B. A stakeholder requirement update
C. A variance analysis showing schedule deviation
D. The project closing report
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, change requests can arise from quality defects, stakeholder requests, performance variances, or risk responses during monitoring and controlling. The closing report documents final results after the project is complete.

questions.question: A responsibility assignment matrix (RAM) maps:
options: A. Project phases to budget allocations
B. Work packages to team members showing who does what
C. Risks to their response strategies
D. Milestones to calendar dates
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a RAM maps project work (from the WBS) to team members or roles, clarifying responsibilities. The RACI chart is the most common type of RAM.

questions.question: A work authorization system ensures:
options: A. All team members have building access
B. Work begins only when properly approved and at the right time
C. The project never exceeds budget
D. Stakeholders can veto any decision
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a work authorization system is a formal procedure for approving and controlling when work begins on work packages. It ensures work is performed in the right sequence and only after proper authorization.

questions.question: A risk report provides:
options: A. Daily task assignments for the team
B. Summary information on overall project risk exposure and individual risk status
C. The project's financial statements
D. Vendor performance evaluations
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, a risk report summarizes overall project risk exposure, status of individual risks, effectiveness of risk responses, new risks identified, and trends. It keeps stakeholders informed about the risk landscape.

questions.question: A lessons learned register should be updated:
options: A. Only at project closure
B. Throughout the project as lessons are identified
C. Only when problems occur
D. Once a year
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, the lessons learned register should be updated continuously throughout the project, not just at closure. Capturing lessons in real-time ensures details are accurate and can be applied to improve current project work.

questions.question: A configuration management plan defines:
options: A. The project's hardware requirements
B. How changes to deliverables and documentation will be tracked and controlled
C. The team's seating arrangement
D. The project methodology selection
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, the configuration management plan defines how changes to project deliverables and documents are identified, controlled, tracked, and audited. It ensures version control and that only approved changes are implemented.

questions.question: A project has BAC=$300K, EV=$150K, AC=$180K. What is the CV?
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, CV = EV - AC = $150,000 - $180,000 = -$30,000. The project is $30K over budget. Negative CV means actual costs exceed the value of work performed.

questions.question: To Complete Performance Index (TCPI) based on BAC tells the PM:
options: A. How fast the team is working
B. The cost efficiency that must be maintained for the remaining work to stay within budget
C. The project's current CPI
D. The number of resources needed
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, TCPI = (BAC - EV) / (BAC - AC). It shows the cost performance required on remaining work to meet the budget. A TCPI > 1.0 means the team must be more efficient than they have been.

questions.question: Integration management ensures:
options: A. All software systems are connected
B. All project management processes and activities work together coherently
C. The team integrates with other departments socially
D. Hardware components are physically assembled
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, integration management coordinates all project management knowledge areas and processes to ensure they work together cohesively. It includes developing the charter, PM plan, directing work, and managing changes.

questions.question: Knowledge management in projects ensures:
options: A. All team members pass certification exams
B. Existing knowledge is leveraged and new knowledge is captured for the organization
C. Only the PM has access to project information
D. Competitors cannot access the project plan
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, knowledge management ensures existing organizational knowledge is used effectively and new knowledge generated by the project is captured, shared, and stored for future benefit.

questions.question: A relational database organizes data into:
options: A. Unstructured text files
B. Tables with rows and columns linked by relationships
C. Blockchain ledgers
D. Binary code only
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, relational databases organize data into tables (relations) with rows (records) and columns (fields). Tables are linked through primary and foreign key relationships. Examples include MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Oracle.

questions.question: High availability in IT systems means:
options: A. Systems are available only during business hours
B. Systems are designed to operate continuously with minimal downtime
C. Only senior staff can access the systems
D. Systems are located at high elevations
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, high availability (HA) designs systems to operate continuously with minimal planned or unplanned downtime, typically targeting 99.9% or higher uptime. Techniques include redundancy, failover, and load balancing.

questions.question: The Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) includes phases such as:
options: A. Mining, smelting, and manufacturing
B. Requirements, design, development, testing, deployment, and maintenance
C. Marketing, sales, and customer support only
D. Hiring, training, and termination
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, the SDLC defines phases for software development: requirements gathering, system design, development/coding, testing/QA, deployment/release, and maintenance/support.

questions.question: FERPA protects:
options: A. Financial records of publicly traded companies
B. Student educational records and privacy
C. Environmental data from pollution monitoring
D. Military classified information
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act) protects the privacy of student education records. IT projects at educational institutions must comply with FERPA when handling student data.

questions.question: A data breach notification requirement mandates that organizations:
options: A. Never disclose security incidents
B. Inform affected individuals and authorities within a specified timeframe after a breach
C. Delete all data after a breach
D. Shut down all IT systems permanently
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, breach notification requirements (mandated by GDPR, state laws, HIPAA) require organizations to notify affected individuals and regulatory authorities within specified timeframes after discovering a data breach.

questions.question: An IT project must comply with ADA requirements. This means ensuring:
options: A. All team members are certified in first aid
B. Digital products are accessible to people with disabilities
C. The project uses only American-made hardware
D. Data is stored only in US data centers
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requires digital products and services to be accessible to people with disabilities. IT projects must consider WCAG guidelines for web accessibility, screen reader compatibility, and other accommodations.

questions.question: COBIT is an IT governance framework that focuses on:
options: A. Agile software development practices
B. Aligning IT goals with business objectives and managing IT risk
C. Physical server rack management
D. Employee onboarding procedures
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, COBIT (Control Objectives for Information and Related Technologies) is a framework for IT management and governance. It helps organizations align IT strategy with business goals, manage risk, and optimize IT resources.

questions.question: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) in project management involves:
options: A. Maximizing profits at any cost
B. Considering the project's impact on society, environment, and ethical standards
C. Only focusing on shareholder returns
D. Ignoring environmental regulations
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, CSR requires organizations and projects to consider their social, environmental, and ethical impact. This includes sustainable practices, fair labor, community engagement, and responsible resource use.

questions.question: Intellectual property (IP) in project management should be:
options: A. Ignored during project planning
B. Identified, protected, and ownership clearly defined in contracts and agreements
C. Shared freely with all competitors
D. Only considered after project closure
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, IP (patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks) must be identified and protected during projects. Ownership should be clearly defined in contracts, especially when working with vendors or creating new innovations.

questions.question: A project steering committee provides:
options: A. Daily task assignments to team members
B. Strategic oversight, governance, and high-level decision-making for the project
C. Technical code reviews
D. Vendor payment processing
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, a steering committee consists of senior stakeholders who provide strategic direction, governance oversight, and make high-level decisions about project priorities, scope changes, and resource allocation.

questions.question: SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework) is designed to:
options: A. Replace Scrum entirely
B. Scale Agile practices across large enterprises with multiple teams
C. Simplify projects to a single team
D. Eliminate the need for project managers
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, SAFe scales Agile practices to enterprise level, coordinating multiple teams working on large products. It organizes teams into Agile Release Trains (ARTs) and provides a structure for portfolio and program-level management.

questions.question: Continuous delivery in Agile means:
options: A. The team works continuously without breaks
B. Code changes are automatically prepared for release to production at any time
C. All features are delivered in the first sprint
D. The project never ends
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, continuous delivery ensures code changes pass through automated build, test, and staging processes so they are always in a release-ready state. Deployment to production can happen at any time with minimal risk.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a responsibility of the project sponsor?
options: A. Providing project funding
B. Writing daily code for the project
C. Removing organizational barriers
D. Making high-level scope decisions
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.1, the project sponsor provides funding, removes barriers, makes strategic decisions, and champions the project. Writing code is a technical team responsibility, not a sponsor duty.

questions.question: The sprint backlog is owned by:
options: A. The Product Owner
B. The Scrum Master
C. The Development Team
D. The Project Sponsor
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.2, the sprint backlog belongs to the Development Team. They select items from the product backlog during sprint planning and determine how to accomplish the work. Only the team can modify the sprint backlog during the sprint.

questions.question: In Scrum, the recommended sprint length is:
options: A. Exactly 6 months
B. 1 to 4 weeks, with 2 weeks being most common
C. 1 day
D. As long as the project requires
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.2, sprints are timeboxed to one month or less, with two weeks being the most common duration. Shorter sprints reduce risk, increase feedback loops, and limit the cost of rework.

questions.question: A work package is:
options: A. The highest level of the WBS
B. The lowest level of the WBS that can be estimated, scheduled, and controlled
C. A shipping container for project materials
D. A collection of project risks
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.3, a work package is the lowest level of the WBS — small enough to be estimated, assigned, and tracked. It represents a deliverable or component that can be assigned to a team member or group.

questions.question: Issue priority should be determined by:
options: A. Who reported the issue first
B. The severity of impact and urgency of resolution
C. The alphabetical order of issue descriptions
D. The project manager's personal preference
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.5, issue priority is based on severity (how much it impacts the project) and urgency (how quickly it needs resolution). High-severity, high-urgency issues are addressed first.

questions.question: A Start-to-Start (SS) dependency means:
options: A. Both activities must finish at the same time
B. The successor can start only when the predecessor starts
C. The predecessor must finish before the successor starts
D. Activities have no relationship
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, a Start-to-Start (SS) dependency means the successor activity can begin only after the predecessor activity has started. Both can run concurrently, but the successor depends on the predecessor starting first.

questions.question: Free float is defined as:
options: A. The amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the project end date
B. The amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting the early start of its successor
C. The total budget available for the project
D. Unused resources on the project
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, free float is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the early start date of any immediate successor activity. Total float considers impact on the project end date.

questions.question: Pull communication is characterized by:
options: A. Information sent directly to recipients via email
B. Information placed in a central location for stakeholders to access when needed
C. Real-time conversations between parties
D. Mandatory attendance at meetings
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.8, pull communication places information in a central location (intranet, shared drive, knowledge base) that recipients can access at their convenience. This is efficient for large audiences needing reference material.

questions.question: Active listening involves:
options: A. Hearing words without processing their meaning
B. Fully concentrating, understanding, responding, and remembering what is said
C. Only listening when the topic is interesting
D. Listening while simultaneously sending emails
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.8, active listening requires full attention, understanding the message, asking clarifying questions, providing feedback, and retaining information. It is essential for effective stakeholder communication.

questions.question: A lessons learned meeting is MOST effective when held:
options: A. Only when the project fails
B. At regular intervals throughout the project and at closure
C. Only at project closure
D. Before the project begins
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.9, lessons learned should be captured throughout the project, not just at closure. Regular retrospectives and periodic reviews ensure knowledge is captured while details are fresh and can be applied immediately.

questions.question: McGregor's Theory Y assumes that:
options: A. Workers are inherently lazy and need constant supervision
B. Workers are self-motivated and enjoy responsibility
C. Workers only respond to financial incentives
D. Workers cannot make decisions independently
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, Theory Y assumes workers are self-motivated, creative, and seek responsibility. Theory X assumes workers are lazy and need supervision. Effective PMs typically operate under Theory Y assumptions.

questions.question: Smoothing (accommodating) as a conflict resolution technique:
options: A. Finds a permanent win-win solution
B. Emphasizes areas of agreement and de-emphasizes differences
C. Forces one party to accept the other's position
D. Avoids the conflict entirely
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, smoothing emphasizes areas of agreement while minimizing differences. It provides temporary relief but does not address the root cause. It is useful for maintaining relationships when the issue is minor.

questions.question: A scoring model uses weighted criteria to:
options: A. Grade team member performance
B. Objectively evaluate and rank potential projects for selection
C. Calculate earned value metrics
D. Determine sprint velocity
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.1, a scoring model assigns weights to evaluation criteria (strategic alignment, ROI, risk, etc.) and scores each candidate project. Projects with the highest weighted scores are selected for the portfolio.

questions.question: A preliminary scope statement developed during discovery includes:
options: A. Detailed work packages and activity sequences
B. High-level project boundaries, major deliverables, and initial constraints
C. Complete resource assignments and schedule
D. Final acceptance criteria and test results
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.1, the preliminary scope statement provides a high-level description of the project scope, major deliverables, assumptions, and constraints. Detailed scope definition occurs during the planning phase.

questions.question: The project charter is typically signed by:
options: A. All team members
B. The project sponsor or initiating authority
C. The QA lead
D. The vendor's account manager
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.2, the project charter is issued by the project sponsor or another initiating authority external to the project. Their signature formally authorizes the project and empowers the project manager.

questions.question: Activity sequencing determines:
options: A. How many resources each activity needs
B. The logical order in which activities must be performed
C. The budget for each activity
D. Who is responsible for each activity
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, activity sequencing identifies the dependencies and logical relationships between activities. It creates the foundation for the network diagram and critical path analysis.

questions.question: A milestone chart shows:
options: A. Detailed activity durations and dependencies
B. Key project events and their planned dates without activity details
C. Resource allocation by team member
D. Budget expenditure over time
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, a milestone chart displays significant project events and their target dates in a simplified format. It provides a high-level schedule overview for executives without the detail of a Gantt chart.

questions.question: Acquiring resources during execution involves:
options: A. Only hiring external contractors
B. Obtaining team members, equipment, materials, and facilities needed for the project
C. Purchasing the project sponsor's approval
D. Renting office space for the PMO
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, acquiring resources involves obtaining the human resources, equipment, materials, supplies, and facilities needed to complete project work. Sources can be internal (staff reassignment) or external (contractors, vendors).

questions.question: A status report during execution typically includes:
options: A. Only good news about the project
B. Current progress, variances from plan, risks, issues, and upcoming milestones
C. Team member personal information
D. Competitor analysis
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, status reports provide a snapshot of project health including progress against baselines, schedule and cost variances, active risks and issues, completed and upcoming milestones, and corrective actions taken.

questions.question: Schedule control involves:
options: A. Only tracking whether the project is on time
B. Monitoring schedule status, managing changes, and taking corrective actions
C. Creating the initial project schedule
D. Assigning resources to activities
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, schedule control monitors the project schedule, identifies variances, evaluates the impact of changes, and implements corrective actions to keep the project on track or adjust the baseline.

questions.question: Cost control in monitoring and controlling includes:
options: A. Setting the initial project budget
B. Tracking expenditures, forecasting costs, and managing budget changes
C. Hiring the finance team
D. Calculating team member salaries
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, cost control monitors budget status, tracks actual expenditures against the cost baseline, forecasts future costs (EAC/ETC), manages change requests that affect budget, and implements corrective actions.

questions.question: A product roadmap shows:
options: A. Physical directions to the project office
B. A high-level strategic plan showing planned features and releases over time
C. Detailed technical architecture diagrams
