D. Individual team member tasks
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a product roadmap is a high-level visual summary showing planned product features, themes, and releases over time. It communicates the product's strategic direction to stakeholders without granular detail.

questions.question: A PMIS (Project Management Information System) is:
options: A. A type of programming language
B. An integrated system of tools and techniques used to collect, store, and distribute project information
C. A single spreadsheet for tracking tasks
D. The project sponsor's personal dashboard
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a PMIS is an information system consisting of tools and techniques used to gather, integrate, and disseminate project management process outputs. Examples include MS Project, Jira, and Asana.

questions.question: A status report differs from a progress report in that a status report:
options: A. Is only sent to the sponsor
B. Provides a snapshot of current project health at a specific point in time
C. Only covers completed work
D. Is written by team members only
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, a status report gives a point-in-time snapshot of current project health (where are we now?). A progress report focuses on what has been accomplished over a period (what did we do since last report?).

questions.question: Actual Cost (AC) in EVM represents:
options: A. The planned budget for work scheduled
B. The total cost actually incurred for work performed to date
C. The value of work completed
D. The estimated cost at project completion
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, Actual Cost (AC) is the total cost actually incurred for work performed during a specific time period. It includes all direct and indirect costs charged to the project for the work accomplished.

questions.question: A project has PV=$200K, EV=$180K, AC=$170K. The project is:
options: A. Over budget and behind schedule
B. Under budget and behind schedule
C. Under budget and ahead of schedule
D. Over budget and ahead of schedule
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, SV = EV-PV = $180K-$200K = -$20K (behind schedule). CV = EV-AC = $180K-$170K = +$10K (under budget). The project is spending less than expected but has completed less work than planned.

questions.question: A firewall in IT networking:
options: A. Cools server hardware to prevent overheating
B. Monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules
C. Accelerates internet connection speed
D. Stores backup data
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, a firewall is a network security device that monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on an organization's security policies. It acts as a barrier between trusted and untrusted networks.

questions.question: Load balancing distributes:
options: A. Project tasks among team members
B. Network traffic across multiple servers to optimize performance and availability
C. Budget across project phases
D. Risk across stakeholders
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, load balancing distributes incoming network traffic across multiple servers so no single server is overwhelmed. It improves application responsiveness, availability, and scalability.

questions.question: The Agile principle 'Welcome changing requirements, even late in development' reflects:
options: A. Poor project planning
B. Agile's embrace of change as a competitive advantage for the customer
C. A lack of scope management
D. The team's inability to say no
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, Agile processes harness change for the customer's competitive advantage. Rather than resisting change, Agile teams have processes that accommodate evolving requirements to deliver maximum value.

questions.question: ISO 27001 is an international standard for:
options: A. Quality management
B. Information security management systems (ISMS)
C. Environmental management
D. Project management
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, ISO 27001 specifies requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an Information Security Management System (ISMS). It provides a framework for managing security risks.

questions.question: Data classification categorizes data based on:
options: A. File size and format
B. Sensitivity level and the impact if disclosed, altered, or destroyed
C. The date it was created
D. The department that owns it
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, data classification categorizes data by sensitivity (public, internal, confidential, restricted) based on the potential impact of unauthorized disclosure, modification, or destruction. It determines security controls required.

questions.question: An Operational Level Agreement (OLA) differs from an SLA in that an OLA:
options: A. Is a legally binding external contract
B. Defines service commitments between internal IT groups within the organization
C. Only applies to cloud services
D. Replaces all vendor contracts
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, an OLA defines the internal service commitments between departments or IT groups within the same organization. SLAs are external agreements between a service provider and customer. OLAs support SLA fulfillment.

questions.question: Portfolio management helps organizations:
options: A. Manage individual project tasks
B. Select and prioritize the right mix of projects aligned with strategic goals
C. Write project charters
D. Conduct sprint planning
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, portfolio management ensures the organization invests in the right projects by selecting, prioritizing, and managing projects and programs as a portfolio aligned with strategic objectives and resource constraints.

questions.question: Ethics in project management requires:
options: A. Maximizing profit regardless of methods
B. Honesty, transparency, fairness, and acting in the best interest of stakeholders
C. Only following rules when being watched
D. Prioritizing the PM's career over project success
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, ethical project management involves honesty, responsibility, respect, fairness, and transparency. PMs must disclose conflicts of interest, protect confidential information, and act in stakeholders' best interests.

questions.question: A balanced matrix organization gives the project manager:
options: A. Full authority over the project budget
B. Shared authority with functional managers
C. No authority at all
D. Authority only over external vendors
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.1, in a balanced matrix, authority is shared equally between the project manager and functional managers. Resources have dual reporting relationships and both managers negotiate priorities.

questions.question: An increment in Scrum is:
options: A. A budget increase request
B. The sum of all completed product backlog items during a sprint plus prior increments
C. A daily status update
D. The number of story points planned
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.2, the increment is the sum of all product backlog items completed during the current sprint and all previous sprints. Each increment must be usable and meet the Definition of Done.

questions.question: The 100% rule for WBS states that:
options: A. All team members must work at 100% capacity
B. The WBS must capture 100% of the project scope, including project management work
C. The project must achieve 100% of its objectives
D. All risks must be mitigated
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.3, the 100% rule requires the WBS to include 100% of the work defined by the project scope. No work should be missing, and no extra work should be included. Each level must account for all work below it.

questions.question: A risk that has been identified but for which no response other than monitoring has been planned is:
options: A. An avoided risk
B. A transferred risk
C. An accepted risk with passive acceptance
D. An exploited risk
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, passive acceptance means the risk is acknowledged and documented but no proactive contingency plan is created. The team monitors the risk and will deal with it if it occurs using workarounds.

questions.question: The 5 Whys technique is used in issue management to:
options: A. Ask five different stakeholders for opinions
B. Drill down to the root cause of a problem by repeatedly asking 'why'
C. Schedule five meetings per week
D. Create five alternative solutions
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.5, the 5 Whys technique asks 'why' iteratively (typically five times) to move beyond symptoms and identify the root cause of a problem. Each answer forms the basis of the next 'why' question.

questions.question: A mandatory dependency is also known as:
options: A. A discretionary dependency
B. A hard logic dependency inherent to the work
C. An external dependency
D. A preference-based dependency
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, mandatory (hard logic) dependencies are inherent to the nature of the work — physically required. For example, foundation must be laid before walls are built. Discretionary dependencies are based on best practices or preferences.

questions.question: Prevention costs in quality management include:
options: A. Rework and scrap costs
B. Training, quality planning, and process documentation
C. Warranty claims and customer complaints
D. Inspection and testing costs
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.7, prevention costs are investments made to prevent defects before they occur, including training, quality planning, process documentation, and proper tools. They are the most cost-effective quality investment.

questions.question: Formal written communication is MOST appropriate when:
options: A. Discussing lunch plans with the team
B. Documenting contractual agreements, official notices, or complex technical specifications
C. Providing quick status updates
D. Brainstorming ideas informally
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.8, formal written communication is used for legal documents, contracts, official correspondence, complex specifications, and records that need an audit trail. Informal methods are better for quick, routine exchanges.

questions.question: Situational leadership suggests that leaders should:
options: A. Use one leadership style for all situations
B. Adapt their leadership style based on the team's maturity and the situation
C. Always use a directive approach
D. Delegate all decisions to the team
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, situational leadership theory states that effective leaders adapt their style (directing, coaching, supporting, delegating) based on the team members' competence and commitment level for each task.

questions.question: Forcing (directing) as a conflict resolution technique:
options: A. Produces a win-win outcome
B. Imposes one viewpoint at the expense of another — a win-lose outcome
C. Avoids the conflict entirely
D. Takes the most time but produces the best results
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, forcing imposes one party's viewpoint over the other, creating a win-lose situation. It should only be used in emergencies when a quick decision is needed or when the issue is critical and non-negotiable.

questions.question: A Request for Quote (RFQ) differs from an RFP in that an RFQ:
options: A. Seeks detailed solution proposals
B. Primarily asks vendors for pricing on well-defined requirements
C. Gathers general vendor information
D. Is used only for internal projects
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.11, an RFQ requests pricing from vendors for clearly defined products or services where requirements are well-established. An RFP seeks detailed proposals including solution approach, methodology, and pricing for complex needs.

questions.question: Technical feasibility assesses whether:
options: A. The project is financially worthwhile
B. The technology needed to build the solution exists and is available
C. The organization will adopt the solution
D. The project has enough team members
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.1, technical feasibility evaluates whether the technology, skills, and infrastructure required to build the solution are available and can be implemented within the project constraints.

questions.question: Operational feasibility determines:
options: A. Whether the project can be built technically
B. Whether the organization can and will use the solution effectively
C. The exact project cost
D. The project schedule
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.1, operational feasibility assesses whether the solution will work within the organization — will users adopt it? Does it align with organizational processes? Can it be supported and maintained long-term?

questions.question: Stakeholder engagement assessment matrix tracks:
options: A. Stakeholder salaries and benefits
B. Current vs desired stakeholder engagement levels (unaware, resistant, neutral, supportive, leading)
C. The project budget by stakeholder
D. Team member work hours
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.2, the stakeholder engagement assessment matrix tracks where each stakeholder currently is (unaware, resistant, neutral, supportive, leading) versus where they need to be. It identifies gaps requiring targeted engagement strategies.

questions.question: A planning package is:
options: A. A completed deliverable
B. A WBS element below the control account but above the work package, with known content but undetermined activities
C. A software tool for project planning
D. The project management plan document
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, a planning package is a WBS component below the control account with known work content but without detailed scheduled activities yet. As the project progresses, planning packages are decomposed into work packages.

questions.question: Defect repair during execution involves:
options: A. Adding new features to the product
B. Formally modifying or replacing a component that does not conform to requirements
C. Cancelling the project
D. Changing the project methodology
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, defect repair involves formally modifying or replacing a non-conforming component to bring it into compliance with requirements or specifications. Defect repairs go through the change control process.

questions.question: Procurement administration during monitoring and controlling involves:
options: A. Selecting the initial vendors
B. Managing procurement relationships, monitoring contract performance, and making changes as needed
C. Writing the RFP
D. Deciding whether to make or buy
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, procurement administration manages vendor relationships, monitors contract performance against SOW and SLA, processes change requests, handles claims and disputes, and reviews invoices for payment.

questions.question: A warranty period after project closure means:
options: A. The project can never be restarted
B. The seller/vendor guarantees the deliverables will function correctly for a specified time
C. Team members are guaranteed employment
D. The budget cannot be audited
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.6, a warranty period is a timeframe after delivery during which the seller agrees to fix defects at no additional cost. It provides assurance to the buyer and may be specified in the contract.

questions.question: Transition to operations during closure involves:
options: A. Starting a new project immediately
B. Transferring project deliverables and knowledge to the team that will support them ongoing
C. Deleting all project files
D. Reassigning the PM to a different department
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.6, transition to operations ensures the deliverables are handed off to the operations or support team with proper documentation, training, and knowledge transfer so they can maintain the product long-term.

questions.question: A mind map helps project teams:
options: A. Calculate earned value metrics
B. Visually brainstorm and organize ideas around a central concept
C. Track time spent on activities
D. Manage vendor contracts
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a mind map is a visual tool that organizes information around a central concept with branching subtopics. It helps with brainstorming, planning, and organizing project ideas and requirements.

questions.question: An influence diagram shows:
options: A. Team member personality types
B. Relationships between variables, decisions, and outcomes in a project
C. The project organizational chart
D. Vendor pricing comparisons
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, an influence diagram is a graphical representation of a decision situation showing variables, decisions, objectives, and their relationships. It helps visualize complex decision-making scenarios.

questions.question: A run chart displays:
options: A. Team member running speed
B. Data points plotted over time to show trends or patterns
C. The project budget allocations
D. Stakeholder communication preferences
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a run chart plots data points in chronological order to reveal trends, shifts, or cycles over time. Unlike control charts, run charts do not include control limits but show the general direction of performance.

questions.question: An action item tracker records:
options: A. Only completed project milestones
B. Specific tasks assigned to individuals with due dates and status
C. The project's financial transactions
D. Team member training certifications
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, an action item tracker documents specific tasks (action items) from meetings or discussions, including the assigned owner, due date, current status, and any notes about progress or completion.

questions.question: Stakeholder management as a knowledge area focuses on:
options: A. Tracking stakeholder salaries
B. Identifying, analyzing, planning, and managing stakeholder engagement throughout the project
C. Removing uncooperative stakeholders
D. Only communicating with the project sponsor
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, stakeholder management involves identifying stakeholders, analyzing their needs and expectations, developing engagement strategies, and managing their engagement throughout the project lifecycle.

questions.question: Resource management as a knowledge area covers:
options: A. Only hiring and firing team members
B. Planning, acquiring, developing, and managing team and physical resources
C. Managing the project budget
D. Scheduling project activities
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, resource management covers identifying, acquiring, managing, and releasing both human resources (team) and physical resources (equipment, materials, facilities) needed for the project.

questions.question: IoT (Internet of Things) refers to:
options: A. A faster version of the internet
B. Physical devices connected to the internet that collect and exchange data
C. A new social media platform
D. An internal company network only
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, IoT refers to the network of physical devices (sensors, appliances, vehicles) embedded with technology that enables them to connect to the internet and exchange data. IT projects may involve IoT integration.

questions.question: Virtualization technology allows:
options: A. Only one operating system per physical server
B. Multiple virtual machines to run on a single physical server
C. Servers to run without electricity
D. Software to run without hardware
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, virtualization creates virtual versions of computing resources (servers, storage, networks), allowing multiple virtual machines to run on one physical server. This improves resource utilization, reduces costs, and enables scalability.

questions.question: In Agile, the primary measure of progress is:
options: A. Percentage of budget spent
B. Working software (or deliverables)
C. Number of documents produced
D. Hours worked by the team
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, the Agile Manifesto states that working software is the primary measure of progress. This principle extends to any Agile project — functional, usable deliverables matter more than documentation or effort metrics.

questions.question: Protected Health Information (PHI) under HIPAA includes:
options: A. Only patient names
B. Any individually identifiable health information including diagnoses, treatments, and medical records
C. Only billing records
D. Public health statistics
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, PHI includes any individually identifiable health information — diagnoses, treatment records, test results, prescriptions, billing information, and any data that can identify a patient combined with health data.

questions.question: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework helps organizations:
options: A. Build mobile applications
B. Manage and reduce cybersecurity risks using five core functions
C. Calculate project earned value
D. Design user interfaces
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework provides five core functions: Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, and Recover. It helps organizations assess and improve their ability to prevent, detect, and respond to cyber threats.

questions.question: ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) considerations in projects include:
options: A. Only financial performance metrics
B. Environmental sustainability, social impact, and ethical governance practices
C. Team member entertainment budgets
D. Marketing campaign effectiveness
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, ESG encompasses environmental factors (carbon footprint, e-waste, energy use), social factors (diversity, labor practices, community impact), and governance factors (ethics, transparency, compliance).

questions.question: Program management differs from project management in that program management:
options: A. Manages a single project
B. Coordinates multiple related projects to achieve strategic benefits
C. Only handles the project budget
D. Reports to the project manager
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, program management coordinates a group of related projects and activities managed together to obtain strategic benefits and control not available from managing them individually. It focuses on program-level objectives.

questions.question: Risk exploitation as a positive risk response means:
options: A. Taking advantage of team members
B. Ensuring an opportunity definitely occurs by taking direct action
C. Ignoring the risk completely
D. Transferring the opportunity to a competitor
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, risk exploitation ensures a positive risk (opportunity) definitely occurs. For example, assigning the most talented team members to ensure a product launches ahead of schedule to capture market share.

questions.question: Appraisal costs in quality management include:
options: A. Training and process documentation
B. Inspections, testing, and quality audits
C. Rework and warranty claims
D. Employee bonuses for quality work
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.7, appraisal costs are incurred to evaluate deliverables and processes for conformance. They include inspections, testing, quality audits, peer reviews, and verification activities.

questions.question: Stakeholders in a project include:
options: A. Only the project team and sponsor
B. Anyone who can affect or be affected by the project
C. Only customers who pay for the product
D. Only senior management
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.1, stakeholders include anyone who may affect, be affected by, or perceive themselves to be affected by the project — including team, sponsor, customers, end users, functional managers, regulators, and community members.

questions.question: A Scrum team is ideally:
options: A. 20-30 people
B. 3-9 developers plus Scrum Master and Product Owner
C. A single developer
D. As large as possible
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.2, the Scrum Guide recommends 10 or fewer people total (typically 3-9 developers plus the Scrum Master and Product Owner). Smaller teams communicate more efficiently and have less coordination overhead.

questions.question: An approved change request becomes:
options: A. A new project
B. An update to the project management plan or baselines
C. A risk in the risk register
D. A lesson learned
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.3, once a change request is approved, it is implemented and may result in updates to the project management plan, baselines (scope, schedule, cost), or other project documents.

questions.question: Residual risk is:
options: A. A risk that is eliminated entirely
B. The risk remaining after a risk response has been implemented
C. A risk that was never identified
D. The total risk of the project
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, residual risk is the risk that remains after risk responses have been applied. Even after mitigation, some level of risk typically persists. Residual risks should be documented and monitored.

questions.question: A lead in scheduling allows:
options: A. The predecessor to start before the successor finishes
B. The successor activity to start before the predecessor finishes
C. Extra time between activities
D. Activities to run in reverse order
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, a lead accelerates the successor activity, allowing it to start before the predecessor is fully complete. For example, starting testing on Module 1 before Module 2 development is finished.

questions.question: Quality metrics define:
options: A. The project's financial performance
B. Specific measurable attributes used to assess quality (defect rates, test coverage, response times)
C. Team member satisfaction scores
D. The number of stakeholders
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.7, quality metrics are specific, measurable criteria that define what quality looks like. Examples include defect density, test coverage percentage, response time, availability, and customer satisfaction scores.

questions.question: Communication barriers include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: A. Language differences and jargon
B. Cultural misunderstandings
C. Clear, simple messaging
D. Information overload
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.8, communication barriers include language differences, jargon, cultural gaps, physical distance, information overload, noise, and filtering. Clear, simple messaging helps overcome barriers — it is not a barrier itself.

questions.question: Withdrawing (avoiding) as a conflict technique:
options: A. Permanently resolves the conflict
B. Retreats from the conflict, leaving it unresolved
C. Produces a win-win outcome
D. Is the most effective long-term strategy
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, withdrawing (avoiding) means retreating from the conflict situation. It does not resolve the issue and may cause it to resurface later. It is appropriate only when the issue is trivial or emotions need time to cool.

questions.question: Economic feasibility evaluates:
options: A. Whether the team has the right skills
B. Whether the project's financial benefits justify its costs
C. Whether the organization will use the product
D. Whether the technology exists
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.1, economic feasibility assesses whether the project's expected financial benefits (ROI, NPV, cost savings) justify its costs and investment. It answers: 'Is this project worth the money?'

questions.question: Project boundaries define:
options: A. The physical walls of the project office
B. What is included in and excluded from the project scope
C. The team's working hours
D. The vendor's delivery area
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.2, project boundaries clearly state what is in scope (included) and out of scope (excluded). Setting boundaries during initiation prevents scope creep and sets clear expectations with stakeholders.

questions.question: The risk management plan defines:
options: A. Individual risk responses for each identified risk
B. How risk management activities will be structured, funded, and performed
C. The complete list of all project risks
D. Insurance policies for the project
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, the risk management plan defines the methodology, roles, budgeting, timing, risk categories, definitions of probability and impact, stakeholder tolerances, and reporting formats for risk management activities.

questions.question: Procurement planning determines:
options: A. The project schedule
B. What to procure, when, how, and from whom
C. Team member responsibilities
D. Quality metrics
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, procurement planning determines which project needs can be met by acquiring products/services externally, the type of contracts to use, the procurement timeline, and the evaluation criteria for vendors.

questions.question: Team development activities during execution may include:
options: A. Only individual performance reviews
B. Training, team building, recognition, and creating a positive team environment
C. Only assigning more work
D. Reducing the team size
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, developing the team improves competencies, interactions, and overall environment. Activities include training, team-building exercises, co-location, recognition/rewards, and establishing ground rules.

questions.question: Risk monitoring during the monitoring and controlling phase involves:
options: A. Ignoring previously identified risks
B. Tracking identified risks, monitoring residual risks, identifying new risks, and evaluating response effectiveness
C. Creating the initial risk register
D. Transferring all risks to the vendor
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, risk monitoring tracks identified risks, monitors triggers, identifies new risks, evaluates the effectiveness of risk responses, and reassesses the overall risk profile throughout the project.

questions.question: Organizational process asset updates during closure include:
options: A. Deleting all project documentation
B. Adding lessons learned, templates, and historical data to the organization's knowledge base
C. Removing the project from the portfolio
D. Cancelling all vendor contracts retroactively
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.6, OPA updates during closure include adding lessons learned, project files, templates, and historical performance data to the organization's knowledge base for use by future projects.

questions.question: A resource calendar shows:
options: A. The project's holiday schedule only
B. When specific resources are available, including working days, shifts, and time off
C. The project milestone dates
D. Stakeholder meeting schedules
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, a resource calendar identifies when each resource (person, equipment) is available for project work. It includes working hours, shifts, holidays, vacations, and other availability constraints.

questions.question: The project management plan is BEST described as:
options: A. A single document listing all project tasks
B. A comprehensive document (or set of subsidiary plans) defining how the project will be executed, monitored, and controlled
C. The project charter
D. The team's daily to-do list
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, the project management plan is the master document defining how the project will be executed, monitored, controlled, and closed. It integrates subsidiary plans for scope, schedule, cost, quality, resources, communication, risk, procurement, and stakeholders.

questions.question: Scope management ensures:
options: A. The project includes all necessary work and only the necessary work
B. The project budget is balanced
C. Team members are properly trained
D. Vendors are selected on time
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, scope management ensures the project includes all the work required to complete the project successfully — and only that work. It prevents scope creep and gold plating through formal change control.

questions.question: Procurement management covers:
options: A. Only the initial vendor selection
B. Planning, conducting, and controlling purchases and acquisitions from outside the project team
C. Internal team resource allocation
D. Quality inspection of deliverables
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, procurement management includes planning procurements, soliciting vendors, selecting sellers, administering contracts, and closing procurements. It covers the entire lifecycle of external acquisitions.

questions.question: A WAN (Wide Area Network) connects:
options: A. Devices within a single room
B. Networks across large geographic distances, often cities or countries
C. Only wireless devices
D. A single computer to a printer
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, a WAN connects networks over large geographic areas, often spanning cities, states, or countries. The internet is the largest WAN. LANs connect devices within a limited area like an office building.

questions.question: A NoSQL database is BEST suited for:
options: A. Strictly structured data with fixed schemas
B. Unstructured or semi-structured data requiring flexibility and scalability
C. Small desktop applications only
D. Financial accounting systems requiring ACID compliance
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, NoSQL databases (MongoDB, Cassandra, DynamoDB) handle unstructured or semi-structured data with flexible schemas. They scale horizontally and are ideal for big data, real-time applications, and content management.

questions.question: Pair programming in XP involves:
options: A. Two teams competing on the same feature
B. Two developers working together at one workstation, taking turns coding
C. Programming only in pairs of files
D. Duplicating code for redundancy
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, pair programming has two developers working at one workstation — one writes code (driver) while the other reviews each line (navigator). They switch roles frequently. It improves code quality and knowledge sharing.

questions.question: Test-driven development (TDD) requires:
options: A. Writing tests after all code is complete
B. Writing automated tests before writing the code they validate
C. Testing only at the end of the sprint
D. Manual testing only
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, TDD follows a cycle: write a failing test first, write the minimum code to pass the test, then refactor. This ensures all code has test coverage and drives design from requirements.

questions.question: Export controls like ITAR restrict:
options: A. Import of consumer electronics
B. Export of defense-related articles, services, and technical data
C. Domestic software sales
D. Cloud computing usage
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, ITAR (International Traffic in Arms Regulations) restricts the export of defense and military-related technologies and data. IT projects involving defense technology must comply with export control regulations.

questions.question: Change management differs from change control in that change management:
options: A. Only tracks changes to documents
B. Focuses on the human and organizational side of implementing change
C. Is the same as version control
D. Only applies to software projects
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, change management focuses on the people side — helping individuals and organizations transition through change (communication, training, resistance management). Change control is the process of managing changes to project deliverables.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of project constraints? (Select TWO)
options: A. Team member preferences for programming languages
B. A government-mandated compliance deadline
C. The project sponsor's favorite color scheme
D. A fixed budget of $2 million
E. The team's preference for Agile
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.1, constraints are factors that limit options. A compliance deadline (time constraint) and fixed budget (cost constraint) are constraints. Team preferences and color schemes are not project constraints.

questions.question: Which of the following are principles of the Agile Manifesto? (Select TWO)
options: A. Maximize the amount of documentation produced
B. Deliver working software frequently
C. Business people and developers must work together daily
D. Follow a detailed plan without deviation
E. Minimize stakeholder involvement
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.2, Agile principles include frequent delivery of working software and daily collaboration between business and development teams. Agile minimizes unnecessary documentation and embraces change rather than rigid plans.

questions.question: Which of the following are risk identification techniques? (Select TWO)
options: A. Brainstorming sessions with the team
B. Resource leveling
C. Expert interviews
D. Fast tracking
E. Schedule compression
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, risk identification techniques include brainstorming, expert interviews, Delphi technique, SWOT analysis, checklists, and document review. Resource leveling, fast tracking, and schedule compression are scheduling techniques.

questions.question: Which of the following are cost estimating techniques? (Select THREE)
options: A. Analogous estimating
B. Risk response planning
C. Parametric estimating
D. Bottom-up estimating
E. Stakeholder identification
F. Vendor negotiation
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, cost estimating techniques include analogous (historical comparison), parametric (statistical relationships), bottom-up (detailed work package estimates), and three-point estimating. Risk response and stakeholder identification are separate processes.

questions.question: Which of the following are activities during the execution phase? (Select THREE)
options: A. Directing and managing project work
B. Creating the project charter
C. Developing the project team
D. Conducting procurements
E. Developing the WBS
F. Calculating the payback period
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, execution activities include directing work, developing the team, managing quality, conducting procurements, managing stakeholder engagement, and implementing approved changes. The charter, WBS, and financial analysis occur in earlier phases.

questions.question: Which of the following are quality management tools? (Select THREE)
options: A. Pareto chart
B. Gantt chart
C. Ishikawa diagram
D. Product backlog
E. Control chart
F. Sprint backlog
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, quality management tools include Pareto charts (80/20 analysis), Ishikawa diagrams (cause-and-effect), control charts (process monitoring), histograms, scatter diagrams, and flowcharts. Gantt charts are scheduling tools; backlogs are Agile artifacts.

questions.question: Which of the following are project closure documents? (Select TWO)
options: A. Project charter
B. Lessons learned report
C. Sprint backlog
D. Final project report
E. Feasibility study
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, closure documents include the final project report, lessons learned report, final acceptance sign-off, and project archive. The charter is created during initiation, sprint backlogs during execution, and feasibility studies during discovery.

questions.question: Which EVM metrics indicate the project is over budget? (Select TWO)
options: A. CPI of 0.85
B. CPI of 1.10
E. SPI of 0.90
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, CPI < 1.0 (0.85) means spending more than value earned — over budget. Negative CV (-$25K) means actual costs exceed earned value — over budget. CPI > 1.0 and positive CV are favorable. SPI measures schedule, not cost.

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of cloud computing? (Select TWO)
options: A. On-demand self-service
B. Requires purchasing physical servers
C. Rapid elasticity and scalability
D. Fixed capacity that cannot change
E. Only available during business hours
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, cloud computing characteristics (per NIST) include on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, and measured service. It eliminates the need to purchase physical servers and offers flexible capacity.

questions.question: Which of the following describe PII (Personally Identifiable Information)? (Select TWO)
options: A. A person's Social Security Number
B. The company's stock ticker symbol
C. An individual's email address
D. A publicly available press release
E. The organization's annual revenue
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, PII is any data that can identify a specific individual, including SSN, email address, phone number, name, date of birth, and biometric data. Company financial data and public press releases are not PII.

questions.question: Which of the following are governance controls? (Select TWO)
options: A. Separation of duties
B. Sprint retrospective
C. Least privilege access
D. Daily standup
E. Product backlog grooming
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, separation of duties and least privilege are governance/security controls that prevent fraud and limit unauthorized access. Sprint retrospectives, daily standups, and backlog grooming are Agile ceremonies.

questions.question: A project manager in a projectized organization reports to:
options: A. A functional department manager
B. The project sponsor or a portfolio/program manager
C. No one — they have complete autonomy
D. The HR department exclusively
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.1, in a projectized organization, PMs have full authority and typically report to the project sponsor, a program manager, or a portfolio manager. Team members report directly to the PM.

questions.question: A team cannot change the sprint goal once the sprint has started in Scrum because:
options: A. The Scrum Master forbids any changes
B. The sprint commitment provides focus and stability for the team
C. It would increase the project budget
D. Sprint goals are never defined
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.2, once a sprint begins, the sprint goal should not be changed because it provides focus and a clear objective. If scope changes are needed, they can be addressed in the next sprint during planning.

questions.question: The difference between scope creep and gold plating is:
options: A. There is no difference
B. Scope creep comes from external pressure; gold plating comes from the team adding unrequested extras
C. Gold plating reduces scope; scope creep adds scope
D. Scope creep is planned; gold plating is unplanned
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.3, scope creep is uncontrolled scope expansion from external stakeholder requests bypassing change control. Gold plating is the team voluntarily adding extras not requested by the customer — both should be avoided.

questions.question: Risk enhancement as a positive risk strategy:
options: A. Eliminates the opportunity entirely
B. Increases the probability or impact of an opportunity
C. Transfers the opportunity to a competitor
D. Accepts the risk without action
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, enhancement increases the probability and/or impact of a positive risk (opportunity). For example, investing in additional marketing to increase the chance of capturing a larger market share.

questions.question: A Finish-to-Finish (FF) dependency means:
options: A. The successor cannot start until the predecessor finishes
B. The successor cannot finish until the predecessor finishes
C. Both activities must start simultaneously
D. Activities have no relationship
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, Finish-to-Finish (FF) means the successor cannot finish until the predecessor finishes. For example, testing cannot finish until documentation is finished if tests rely on final documentation.

questions.question: Internal failure costs include:
options: A. Customer warranty claims
B. Rework and scrap identified before delivery to the customer
C. Quality training programs
D. Quality audits
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.7, internal failure costs occur when defects are found before delivery — including rework, scrap, re-testing, and downtime. External failure costs occur when defects reach the customer (warranty, liability, reputation damage).

questions.question: A facilitator in meetings is responsible for:
options: A. Making all decisions for the group
B. Guiding discussion, ensuring participation, and keeping the meeting on track
C. Taking meeting minutes
D. Providing technical expertise on all topics
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.9, the facilitator guides the meeting process — ensuring all voices are heard, keeping discussions focused on the agenda, managing time, and helping the group reach decisions without imposing their own views.

questions.question: Legitimate power comes from:
options: A. Personal charisma and likability
B. A person's formal position or title in the organization
C. Technical expertise
D. The ability to give bonuses
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, legitimate power comes from a person's formal position or authority within the organization. A VP has legitimate power over directors. In a projectized organization, the PM has legitimate power over the team.

questions.question: A Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) in procurement:
options: A. Defines the project schedule
B. Protects confidential information shared between parties during a business relationship
C. Sets the final contract price
D. Replaces the project charter
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.11, an NDA is a legal agreement that protects confidential information shared between parties. It ensures vendors and team members do not disclose proprietary information, trade secrets, or sensitive project details.

questions.question: A market analysis during discovery helps determine:
options: A. The project schedule
B. Whether there is demand for the product and how competitors are positioned
C. Team member skill gaps
D. The risk register entries
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.1, market analysis assesses demand for the proposed product/service, competitive landscape, target audience, and market trends. It informs the business case and helps justify the project investment.

questions.question: Initial team identification during initiation involves:
options: A. Hiring all project team members
B. Identifying key team members and roles needed to begin planning
C. Completing all team training
D. Conducting performance reviews
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.2, during initiation, key team members and roles are identified (PM, key SMEs, leads) to begin planning. The full team is acquired during execution. Initial identification ensures the right expertise is available for planning.

questions.question: A communication plan should be reviewed and updated:
options: A. Only at project closure
B. Regularly throughout the project as stakeholder needs change
C. Once during initiation and never again
D. Only when problems occur
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, the communication plan should be reviewed and updated periodically as stakeholders change, new information needs arise, or communication methods prove ineffective. It is a living document.

questions.question: Conducting procurements during execution involves:
options: A. Planning what to procure
B. Obtaining seller responses, selecting sellers, and awarding contracts
C. Closing vendor contracts
D. Writing the RFP
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, conducting procurements involves obtaining vendor responses (bids/proposals), evaluating them against criteria, selecting the best vendor, and awarding the contract. RFP writing occurs during planning.

questions.question: A performance report synthesizes:
options: A. Only positive project outcomes
B. Work performance information into comprehensive reports for stakeholder decision-making
C. Team member personality profiles
D. Vendor marketing materials
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, performance reports compile work performance information into comprehensive documents for stakeholder review. They include status, progress, forecasts, variance analysis, and earned value metrics.

questions.question: Final acceptance during closure requires:
options: A. Only the PM's signature
B. Formal sign-off from the customer or sponsor confirming deliverables meet requirements
C. A team vote
D. Vendor approval
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.6, final acceptance is the formal acknowledgment by the customer or sponsor that project deliverables meet the defined acceptance criteria. It is documented and triggers the administrative closure process.

questions.question: A PERT chart differs from a Gantt chart in that a PERT chart:
options: A. Shows task durations as horizontal bars
B. Emphasizes task dependencies and the flow of activities in a network format
C. Is used only in Agile projects
D. Shows resource allocation
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) charts display activities as a network showing dependencies and critical path. Gantt charts show activities as horizontal bars on a timeline. PERT emphasizes relationships; Gantt emphasizes schedule.

questions.question: The scope management plan describes:
options: A. The project budget allocation
B. How scope will be defined, validated, and controlled throughout the project
C. Team member responsibilities
D. The project risk responses
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, the scope management plan defines how scope will be defined, developed, monitored, controlled, and verified. It includes processes for creating the WBS, handling scope changes, and validating deliverables.

questions.question: Schedule management as a knowledge area includes:
options: A. Only creating the Gantt chart
B. Defining activities, sequencing them, estimating durations, developing and controlling the schedule
C. Managing the project budget
D. Conducting quality audits
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, schedule management includes defining activities, sequencing activities, estimating activity durations, developing the schedule, and controlling the schedule throughout the project.

questions.question: Cost management as a knowledge area covers:
options: A. Only tracking expenditures
B. Planning, estimating, budgeting, funding, financing, managing, and controlling costs
C. Setting team member salaries
D. Negotiating vendor contracts
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, cost management encompasses planning cost management, estimating costs, determining the budget, and controlling costs to ensure the project is completed within the approved budget.

questions.question: A data warehouse is:
options: A. A physical storage room for servers
B. A centralized repository that stores integrated data from multiple sources for analysis
C. A type of NoSQL database
D. A backup tape storage system
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, a data warehouse is a centralized repository that integrates data from multiple sources for reporting and analysis. It supports business intelligence, trend analysis, and decision-making.

questions.question: Microservices architecture designs applications as:
options: A. A single monolithic codebase
B. A collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services
C. One large database
D. A series of stored procedures
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, microservices architecture breaks applications into small, independent services that can be developed, deployed, and scaled independently. Each service handles a specific business function and communicates via APIs.

questions.question: The Agile principle of 'sustainable pace' means:
options: A. The team should work as fast as possible
B. Teams should maintain a constant, sustainable work pace indefinitely without burnout
C. Sprints should get shorter over time
D. Only senior developers should set the pace
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, the sustainable pace principle states that Agile processes promote sustainable development. Sponsors, developers, and users should maintain a constant pace indefinitely, avoiding overtime and burnout.

questions.question: A compliance audit in an IT project verifies:
options: A. That the project is under budget
B. That the project adheres to applicable laws, regulations, and organizational policies
C. That the team is working overtime
D. That all risks have been eliminated
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, compliance audits verify that the project, its processes, and deliverables conform to applicable regulatory requirements, industry standards, and organizational policies. Non-compliance can result in fines or legal action.

questions.question: Configuration management in IT governance tracks:
options: A. Team member locations
B. IT assets, their versions, relationships, and authorized changes
C. The project's marketing strategy
D. Customer satisfaction scores
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, configuration management identifies, controls, and tracks IT assets (hardware, software, documentation) and their versions, ensuring only authorized changes are made and a complete audit trail exists.

questions.question: Progressive elaboration during planning means:
options: A. The plan is finalized immediately and never changed
B. Planning details increase as more information becomes available
C. The team progressively reduces the scope
D. Only the budget is elaborated over time
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, progressive elaboration refines and adds detail to the project management plan as the project progresses and more information is gathered. Early high-level estimates are replaced with detailed plans.

questions.question: Managing communications during execution ensures:
options: A. All emails are copied to every stakeholder
B. The right information reaches the right stakeholders at the right time
C. Only the PM communicates externally
D. Communication occurs only through formal channels
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, managing communications creates, distributes, stores, retrieves, and disposes of project information in accordance with the communication plan, ensuring stakeholders receive timely and relevant information.

questions.question: Quality management as a knowledge area ensures:
options: A. The team works the fastest possible speed
B. The project satisfies the needs for which it was undertaken by meeting quality requirements
C. All defects are hidden from the customer
D. The cheapest materials are used
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, quality management ensures the project and its deliverables meet the defined quality standards and stakeholder expectations. It covers quality planning, quality assurance, and quality control.

questions.question: Risk management as a knowledge area includes:
options: A. Only avoiding all risks
B. Planning, identifying, analyzing, responding to, and monitoring risks
C. Eliminating all uncertainty from the project
D. Only tracking positive risks
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, risk management includes planning risk management, identifying risks, performing qualitative and quantitative analysis, planning risk responses, implementing responses, and monitoring risks throughout the project.

questions.question: Communication management as a knowledge area ensures:
options: A. The team has the best communication devices
B. Timely and appropriate planning, collection, creation, distribution, storage, and management of project information
C. All conversations are recorded
D. Only written communication is used
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, communication management includes planning communications, managing communications, and monitoring communications to ensure project information is timely, accurate, and reaches the right stakeholders.

questions.question: A discretionary dependency is based on:
options: A. Physical or legal requirements that cannot be changed
B. Best practices, preferences, or lessons learned from past projects
C. External regulatory mandates
D. Equipment limitations
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, discretionary (soft logic/preferred logic) dependencies are based on best practices, historical preference, or team experience. They can be adjusted during schedule compression techniques like fast tracking.

questions.question: An external dependency involves:
options: A. Dependencies within the project team only
B. A relationship between project activities and non-project activities
C. Dependencies between WBS elements
D. Team member skill dependencies
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, external dependencies involve relationships between project activities and external factors outside the project's control, such as government approvals, vendor deliveries, or environmental permits.

questions.question: Quality control during monitoring and controlling includes:
options: A. Creating the quality management plan
B. Inspecting deliverables and measuring results against quality standards
C. Defining quality metrics
D. Selecting quality tools
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, quality control involves inspecting deliverables, testing products, measuring results against quality standards, and documenting defects. It verifies that deliverables meet the acceptance criteria.

questions.question: Communication monitoring ensures:
options: A. All team members have phones
B. Communication needs of stakeholders are being met and the communication plan is effective
C. Only the PM receives project updates
D. All meetings are cancelled
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, monitoring communications evaluates whether the communication plan is effective, stakeholder information needs are being met, and adjustments are needed to the communication approach.

questions.question: A project has BAC=$500K, EV=$200K, AC=$250K, PV=$300K. The SV is:
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, SV = EV - PV = $200K - $300K = -$100K. The project is behind schedule — $100K worth of planned work has not been completed. The negative SV indicates the team has earned less value than planned.

questions.question: Using the same data (BAC=$500K, EV=$200K, AC=$250K), the EAC is:
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, CPI = EV/AC = $200K/$250K = 0.80. EAC = BAC/CPI = $500K/0.80 = $625K. The project is expected to cost $625K — $125K over the original $500K budget if current spending efficiency continues.

questions.question: An internal stakeholder is someone who:
options: A. Works outside the organization
B. Is a member of the performing organization such as a team member or executive
C. Is a customer or end user only
D. Has no influence on the project
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.1, internal stakeholders are within the performing organization — employees, managers, executives, and team members. External stakeholders include customers, regulators, suppliers, and the general public.

questions.question: When using a hybrid approach, the planning phase might use Waterfall while development uses Agile. This is called:
options: A. Pure Agile
B. Pure Waterfall
C. Water-Scrum-Fall
D. Six Sigma
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.2, Water-Scrum-Fall is a hybrid approach where initial planning and requirements use Waterfall's sequential approach, development iterations use Scrum/Agile, and deployment follows a traditional release process.

questions.question: Integrated change control is performed:
options: A. Only during the planning phase
B. Throughout the entire project from initiation through closure
C. Only when the customer requests changes
D. Only during project closure
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.3, integrated change control is performed from project initiation through closure. It reviews all change requests, approves or rejects changes, manages changes to baselines, and coordinates changes across knowledge areas.

questions.question: A risk category groups risks by:
options: A. Their monetary value only
B. Common sources such as technical, external, organizational, or project management
C. The team member who identified them
D. The date they were identified
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, risk categories organize risks by common sources. Typical categories include technical (technology, requirements), external (regulatory, market), organizational (resources, funding), and project management (estimation, planning).

questions.question: When an issue is resolved, the PM should:
options: A. Delete it from the issue log
B. Update the issue log to reflect the resolution and lessons learned
C. File it with the risk register
D. Ignore it going forward
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.5, resolved issues should be updated in the issue log with the resolution, date closed, and any lessons learned. Keeping the history helps track patterns and provides documentation for future reference.

questions.question: External failure costs include:
options: A. Rework identified during internal testing
B. Warranty claims, returns, and reputation damage from defects reaching customers
C. Quality planning and training
D. Inspection equipment maintenance
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.7, external failure costs occur when defects are found by customers — warranty claims, product returns, liability costs, loss of reputation, and lost future business. These are the most expensive quality costs.

questions.question: A status meeting is held to:
options: A. Conduct team building exercises
B. Review current project progress, issues, and upcoming milestones
C. Celebrate project completion
D. Negotiate vendor contracts
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.9, status meetings review current project progress against the plan, discuss active issues and risks, report on milestones, and identify upcoming tasks. They keep the team and stakeholders aligned.

questions.question: Coercive power is based on:
options: A. The ability to give rewards
B. The ability to punish or impose negative consequences
C. Technical expertise
D. Personal likability
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, coercive power comes from the ability to punish, withhold rewards, or impose negative consequences. It is considered the least effective form of power and should be used sparingly as a last resort.

questions.question: Reward power is based on:
options: A. The leader's personal charisma
B. The ability to provide desired rewards such as bonuses, promotions, or recognition
C. The leader's technical knowledge
D. The leader's formal title
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, reward power comes from the ability to give desired rewards — bonuses, promotions, recognition, desirable assignments. It can be effective for motivation but may not build long-term commitment.

questions.question: A problem statement in the business case describes:
options: A. The project schedule
B. The specific business problem or opportunity the project addresses
C. Team member qualifications
D. Vendor selection criteria
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.1, the problem statement clearly articulates the business problem, pain point, or opportunity that the project aims to address. It sets the context for why the project is needed and what success looks like.

questions.question: Governance structure established during initiation defines:
options: A. The technical architecture
B. Decision-making authority, escalation paths, and reporting relationships
C. The coding standards
D. The testing framework
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.2, the governance structure defines who has decision-making authority, escalation paths for issues, reporting relationships, review/approval processes, and oversight responsibilities for the project.

questions.question: A baseline in project management is:
options: A. A rough estimate that can change at any time
B. An approved version of a plan used as a reference for measuring performance
C. The first draft of any document
D. The lowest acceptable quality level
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, a baseline is the approved version of scope, schedule, or cost that serves as the reference point for measuring and comparing actual performance. Changes require formal change control.

questions.question: Implementing approved changes during execution requires:
options: A. Skipping impact analysis
B. Following the change management plan to ensure changes are properly implemented
C. Ignoring the change control board's decision
D. Only verbal communication to the team
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, approved changes must be implemented following the change management plan. This includes updating relevant baselines, communicating changes to the team and stakeholders, and verifying the change was implemented correctly.

questions.question: Scope control prevents:
options: A. Risks from occurring
B. Unauthorized changes to the project scope
C. Team members from taking vacation
D. Budget increases
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.5, scope control monitors scope status, manages changes to the scope baseline, and prevents unauthorized modifications. It ensures all scope changes go through the formal change control process.

questions.question: A project evaluation at closure assesses:
options: A. Only the team's technical skills
B. Whether the project achieved its objectives, delivered on time/budget, and met quality standards
C. The vendor's future product roadmap
D. The next project's requirements
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.6, project evaluation reviews overall performance — did it meet objectives, was it on time and within budget, did deliverables meet quality standards, were stakeholders satisfied, and what can be improved?

questions.question: A collaboration tool in project management includes:
options: A. Only email
B. Shared workspaces, instant messaging, video conferencing, and document sharing platforms
C. Only physical whiteboards
D. Only the project charter
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.1, collaboration tools include shared workspaces (SharePoint, Confluence), instant messaging (Slack, Teams), video conferencing (Zoom), document sharing, and project management platforms (Jira, Asana).

questions.question: Requirements documentation serves as:
options: A. A daily task list for developers
B. A detailed description of what the project must deliver to satisfy stakeholder needs
C. The project budget
D. Team member performance goals
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.2, requirements documentation captures the detailed description of product/project requirements — functional, non-functional, technical, and business requirements that must be met for stakeholder satisfaction.

questions.question: A project has PV=$400K, EV=$350K, AC=$380K. Is the project on budget and on schedule?
options: A. Over budget and ahead of schedule
B. Under budget and behind schedule
C. Over budget and behind schedule
D. Under budget and ahead of schedule
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, CV = EV-AC = $350K-$380K = -$30K (over budget). SV = EV-PV = $350K-$400K = -$50K (behind schedule). The project is both over budget and behind schedule.

questions.question: A LAN (Local Area Network) connects:
options: A. Networks across countries
B. Devices within a limited area such as an office or building
C. Only wireless devices worldwide
D. Satellites and ground stations
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, a LAN connects devices within a limited geographic area — typically a single building, office, or campus. It enables shared access to resources like printers, files, and internet connections.

questions.question: Backup strategies for data protection include:
options: A. Only full backups daily
B. Full, incremental, and differential backups with varying frequencies
C. Never backing up data
D. Only printing hard copies
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, backup strategies include full backups (all data), incremental (only changes since last backup), and differential (changes since last full backup). Organizations use combinations based on recovery time objectives.

questions.question: The Agile principle of face-to-face communication states it is:
options: A. Optional and rarely useful
B. The most efficient and effective method of conveying information within a development team
C. Only for conflict resolution
D. Less effective than email
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, the Agile Manifesto principle states that face-to-face conversation is the most efficient and effective method of conveying information. Even with remote teams, real-time interactive communication is preferred.

questions.question: Continuous integration requires developers to:
options: A. Work in isolation for weeks before sharing code
B. Merge code changes into a shared repository frequently with automated builds and tests
C. Only integrate code at the end of the project
D. Skip testing to save time
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.2, continuous integration requires developers to merge code changes into a shared repository frequently (ideally daily). Automated builds and tests verify each integration, catching issues early.

questions.question: A project processing European customer data must comply with GDPR's 'right to be forgotten' which means:
options: A. The organization can forget its contractual obligations
B. Individuals can request their personal data be deleted
C. Project documents can be discarded
D. The team can ignore compliance requirements
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.3, GDPR's right to erasure (right to be forgotten) allows EU residents to request deletion of their personal data. IT systems must support this capability, impacting project design decisions.

questions.question: An audit trail in IT governance provides:
options: A. A path through a hiking trail
B. A chronological record of system activities that can be reviewed to reconstruct events
C. A list of project milestones
D. Team member attendance records
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, an audit trail is a chronological record of system activities (logins, changes, transactions) that enables reconstruction of events for security, compliance, and troubleshooting purposes.

questions.question: In Kanban, the primary focus is on:
options: A. Time-boxed iterations like sprints
B. Continuous flow of work and visualizing the workflow
C. Fixed roles like Product Owner and Scrum Master
D. Predefined ceremonies and events
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.2, Kanban focuses on continuous workflow rather than time-boxed iterations. Work items flow through the board as capacity allows, with WIP limits preventing overload. There are no predefined roles or ceremonies.

questions.question: A Start-to-Finish (SF) dependency is the LEAST common and means:
options: A. The successor must finish before the predecessor can start
B. The successor cannot finish until the predecessor starts
C. Both activities must start together
D. Both activities must finish together
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, Start-to-Finish (SF) means the successor cannot finish until the predecessor has started. It is the rarest dependency type. Example: a new security system (successor) cannot go offline until the replacement system (predecessor) starts.

questions.question: The scope management plan describes how:
options: A. Budget will be allocated across departments
B. Project scope will be defined, validated, documented, and controlled
C. Team members will be recruited
D. Risks will be identified and analyzed
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.3, the scope management plan outlines how project scope will be defined, developed, monitored, controlled, and verified. It provides guidance for creating the scope statement, WBS, and managing scope changes.

questions.question: Knowledge transfer during execution involves:
options: A. Deleting all project documentation
B. Sharing expertise, information, and skills among team members to build capability
C. Only sending emails about deadlines
D. Restricting information to the PM only
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.4, knowledge transfer during execution involves sharing expertise among team members through mentoring, training, documentation, and cross-functional collaboration. It builds team capability and reduces key-person risk.

questions.question: The make-or-buy analysis compares:
options: A. Two vendors' proposals
B. The cost and benefits of producing work internally versus outsourcing it
C. Different project methodologies
D. Quality standards across industries
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 3.3, make-or-buy analysis evaluates whether work should be done in-house (make) or outsourced to a vendor (buy). It considers cost, capacity, expertise, risk, strategic value, and intellectual property concerns.

questions.question: A web service allows:
options: A. Only browsing web pages
B. Applications to communicate over the internet using standardized protocols
C. Physical server maintenance
D. Printing web pages
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.1, web services enable applications to communicate over the internet using standardized protocols (REST, SOAP). They allow different systems to exchange data regardless of their underlying technology.

questions.question: Change control vs change management: change control manages:
options: A. People's reactions to organizational change
B. Formal processes for requesting, reviewing, approving, and implementing changes to project deliverables
C. Employee training programs
D. Team morale
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 4.4, change control is the formal process of managing changes to project deliverables, documents, and baselines. It includes change requests, impact analysis, CCB review, and implementation tracking. Change management focuses on the people side.

questions.question: A project phase is:
options: A. The same as a milestone
B. A collection of logically related activities culminating in the completion of one or more deliverables
C. A single task in the WBS
D. The project sponsor's decision period
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.1, a project phase is a collection of logically related activities that culminates in one or more deliverables. Phases are sequential or overlapping and typically end with a phase gate review.

questions.question: Backlog prioritization is the responsibility of:
options: A. The Scrum Master
B. The Product Owner
C. The Development Team
D. The Project Sponsor
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.2, the Product Owner is solely responsible for prioritizing the product backlog. They order items by value, risk, dependencies, and business need to maximize the value delivered by the team.

questions.question: A change request should document:
options: A. Only the desired change
B. The change description, reason, impact assessment, and urgency
C. Only who requested the change
D. The team's opinion about the change
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.3, a formal change request documents the proposed change, its justification/reason, the requestor, impact on scope/schedule/cost/quality, urgency level, and recommended action for the CCB to evaluate.

questions.question: A risk breakdown structure (RBS) organizes risks by:
options: A. Alphabetical order
B. Categories and subcategories in a hierarchical structure
C. Budget impact only
D. The date they were identified
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.4, the RBS is a hierarchical representation of risks organized by categories (technical, external, organizational, project management) and subcategories. It helps ensure comprehensive risk identification.

questions.question: Activities on the critical path have:
options: A. The most float
B. Zero float — any delay directly extends the project end date
C. Unlimited duration flexibility
D. The highest budget allocation
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.6, critical path activities have zero total float — any delay to these activities directly delays the project completion date. The critical path determines the minimum project duration.

questions.question: A quality audit is:
options: A. A financial review of the project budget
B. A structured review to determine if project activities comply with policies and processes
C. A team performance evaluation
D. A vendor price comparison
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.7, a quality audit is a structured, independent review to verify that project activities comply with organizational and project policies, processes, and procedures. It identifies gaps and best practices.

questions.question: A project has 15 team members. How many communication channels exist?
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.8, using n(n-1)/2: 15(14)/2 = 210/2 = 105 communication channels. This demonstrates why larger teams face exponentially greater communication complexity.

questions.question: During the performing stage of team development:
options: A. Team members are still learning each other's roles
B. The team operates at peak efficiency with minimal supervision
C. Conflicts are at their highest level
D. The team is being disbanded
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 1.10, during performing, the team functions as a cohesive unit with high productivity, mutual trust, and effective collaboration. Team members are interdependent and require minimal oversight from the PM.

questions.question: Organizational readiness assessment evaluates:
options: A. The budget for office renovations
B. Whether the organization is prepared to implement and sustain the project outcomes
C. The availability of parking spaces
D. The project schedule only
questions.explanation: Per PK0-005 objective 2.1, organizational readiness assesses whether the organization has the capacity, culture, processes, and resources to implement and sustain the proposed project outcomes. It identifies potential resistance and gaps.

questions.question: High-level risk identification during initiation:
options: A. Creates the complete risk register with all responses
B. Identifies major risks that could impact project feasibility and includes them in the charter
C. Eliminates all project risks
D. Is performed only by external consultants
